El proceso de corte es, por el contrario, sencillo: desde el punto de vista del programa, se trata simplemente de piezas de modelo comunes, mientras que al proceso de procesamiento del mineral se le han asignado atributos de diferentes dimensiones, como la dureza, la tenacidad y la resistencia a los ácidos; además, se está desarrollando la mecánica del tratamiento térmico.El objetivo de «Lamprey» es que cada herramienta tenga su razón de ser. Según su visión, el procesamiento de minerales ocupará entre el 60 % y el 70 % del tiempo de los jugadores, el corte, un 10 %, y el resto se dedicará a la creación de accesorios.

Aquí, la veracidad cede el paso a la jugabilidad. A la hora de diseñar las características específicas de los minerales, Lampworm da más importancia a que sean intuitivas; por ejemplo, el diamante y el corindón deben ser más duros, sin necesidad de reproducir al pie de la letra los parámetros físicos de la realidad.En cuanto a la fosforita, conocida entre los jugadores como «el señor Rompedor», y que es objeto de frecuentes debates, esto se debe a la serie de manga «El país de las gemas»: en «Lamprey», se quería que este mineral tan frágil causara una gran impresión en el juego.

La mayor concesión se produjo en el sistema de calidad: en la primera prueba, el juego no contaba con una clasificación de calidad, sino que definía directamente la calidad de las gemas mediante propiedades reales, como el índice de daños.Más tarde, Lampworm se dio cuenta del problema que planteaba este diseño: cuando los jugadores compartían sus logros en las redes sociales, una frase como «He conseguido una gema de calidad perfecta» se entendía a la primera, mientras que «He conseguido una gema con un grado de daño igual a cero» resultaba incomprensible.

Hoy en día, las gemas del juego se clasifican en cinco categorías: de mala calidad, normal, buena, excelente y perfecta; el precio a pagar es que, en ocasiones, aparece una «calidad perfecta» con una tasa de rotura del 90 %. Él reconoce que esto no es del todo realista, pero ningún jugador rechazaría la sensación de logro que proporcionan las etiquetas de calidad de todos los colores que se ven en el almacén.

La «adicción» de los jugadores proviene de otro conjunto de diseños: en un principio, «Lamprey» se inspiraba en títulos de menor envergadura, como «Fishing Vessel: Dark Currents»; sin embargo, tras introducir la mecánica de las piedras de lotería y el sistema de calidad, se añadieron la profundidad del coleccionismo y el juego de riesgos, lo que él describe como «un efecto multiplicador».En cuanto a la adicción de los jugadores, su conclusión es muy directa: «Se aprovechan de las debilidades humanas, no hay mucho más que decir. A todo el mundo le gusta apostar y coleccionar objetos brillantes de diferentes calidades».

Opiniones de los usuarios en Xiaohongshu

Desde el lanzamiento de la versión de prueba, se siguen realizando ajustes. El juego incluye cuestionarios y un canal para informar de fallos, y al finalizar cada prueba se lleva a cabo una ronda completa de recopilación de opiniones de los jugadores. Los jugadores pueden ponerse en contacto con él directamente a través de los grupos de QQ en China y de Discord en el extranjero.

Al final del artículo, «Lamprey» pidió a «Game Teahouse» que transmitiera dos mensajes a los jugadores.

En primer lugar, en cuanto a los elementos de terror del juego, durante la demo, algunos jugadores se sintieron desanimados por la atmósfera del juego,Lamprey se ha comprometido a crear un modo de terror «suave», en el que los sucesos especialmente inquietantes, como las polillas gigantes o los apagones, se tratarán de forma más moderada. Sin embargo, este modo implica demasiada lógica, por lo que quizá no esté listo para el lanzamiento de la versión oficial, aunque se añadirá lo antes posible posteriormente.

En cuanto a eliminar por completo los elementos de terror, Lampworm admite que es muy difícil de lograr, ya que algunos elementos están ligados a la mecánica del juego; por ejemplo, los ojos que crecen en los minerales: sería una pena eliminarlos. Al mismo tiempo, subraya que, incluso en el modo normal del juego, no habrá sustos repentinos ni persecuciones, por lo que los jugadores pueden estar tranquilos.

En segundo lugar, en cuanto al problema de mareos que han mencionado algunos jugadores, Lampe Worm afirma que ha recibido más quejas al respecto que sobre el terror, y asegura que en la versión oficial se incluirá un modo de desplazamiento rápido mediante teletransporte.

Por supuesto, a los jugadores no solo les preocupan estas dos cuestiones; por ejemplo, se ha hablado mucho del sistema económico: en la versión de prueba, los accesorios creados con esmero a veces no se venden por más que las piedras en bruto.La explicación de Lampworm al respecto es que el valor de los accesorios radica más bien en la reputación que otorgan y en las mejoras de atributos que proporcionan; los valores concretos se perfeccionarán aún más en versiones posteriores. En cuanto al problema de que, en las últimas fases del juego, no se pueda gastar el dinero, también se resolverá en la versión oficial, ya que aún hay una gran cantidad de opciones de mejora, equipamiento y herramientas avanzadas que no se han desbloqueado.

Ya se han sentado las bases para proyectos más ambiciosos; esa visión del mundo con tintes de alquimia es fruto de la experiencia acumulada en proyectos anteriores, y *El joyero del abismo* «supone, en cierto modo, un punto de partida».

title: ウィッシュリスト登録数17万件、中国発のインディーゲームからまたも隠れたダークホースが登場
text:
この1ヶ月余りの間、小紅書では次々とユーザーが自作のジュエリー作品を投稿し続けている。写真に写る指輪やネックレスには、色や輝きが異なる宝石が散りばめられており、そのデザインは上品なものから奇抜なものまで様々だ。中には、宝石を組み合わせて「巨大な剣」を作り上げた人もいるほどだ。
これらのアクセサリーはすべて、同じゲーム『地淵の宝石職人』から生まれたものです。
このゲームの正式版はまだ発売されていませんが、Steamで公開された無料体験版にはすでに560件以上のユーザーレビューが寄せられており、高評価率は86％で、プラットフォームから「特に好評」と評価されています。また、ウィッシュリスト登録数は17万件に達しています。9月末には、2026年indiePlay中国インディーゲームコンテストの「最優秀デザイン賞」にもノミネートされました。
そして、これらの数字は、たった1人で構成される「開発チーム」によるものだ。
01
まずテンセントで1年間働いた
『地淵の宝石職人』の作者である灯蠕虫は、テンセントでゲーム業界への第一歩を踏み出した。大学卒業後、同社のパブリッシング部門でゲームプランナーとして勤務した。
この経験は1年にも満たなかったが、彼のゲームに対する理解を一変させた。学生時代、灯蠕虫もいくつかのインディーズゲームを制作していたが、当時は自己表現を重視しており、作品が売れるかどうかはあまり気にしていなかった。しかし、パブリッシング業務に携わる中で、彼は初めてプロジェクトの商業的価値について真剣に考えるようになった。
2023年9月、灯蠕虫は退職を決意した。その時点で入社してまだ1年も経っていなかった。彼は、当初の計画ではまず数年働いて資金を貯め、その後インディーズゲームの開発を始めるつもりだったと振り返るが、インディーズ開発にかかる費用は実際には限られていると判断し、予定より早く行動に移した。
退職後、彼が手掛けた最初のプロジェクトは、香水と錬金術をテーマにしたもので、『スルタンのゲーム』や『密教シミュレーター』に近いゲームプレイのカードゲームだった。このプロジェクトは1年余り続いたが、次第に頓挫してしまった。
ランプワームのアトリエ
彼にはインスピレーションを記録する習慣があり、ここ数年、実現可能だと感じ、かつやりたいと思ったアイデアはすべて「ライトワーム」がインスピレーション・データベースに記録し、開発の優先順位に従って並べ替えている。
一部のクリエイティブなテーマは同じ創作コンセプトを共有しており、灯蠕虫はそれを「復魅」と総称している。これは、現実世界において美しく、情緒的な価値はあるものの、実用性のないものをゲームの世界観に取り入れ、そこに実用的な機能を持たせることを意味する。香水を例に挙げると、現実世界の香水、宝石、タトゥーといったものは、人々の美や記憶、アイデンティティに対する想像を宿している一方で、別の視点から見れば、単なる情緒的価値しか持たない「偽物」に過ぎない。しかし彼は、ゲームの中でこうした想像を現実のものにしたいと考えている。香水は単なる香りではなく、人の肉体さえも変え、さらには魂にまで作用し得るものなのだ。
2024年10月、彼はインスピレーションの宝庫から「宝石」というテーマを選び出し、「スポットライト」への参加に向けて『地淵の宝石職人』の最初のバージョンを作成した。
02
まず遊び方を決めてから、物語を作り上げる
体験版が公開されると、すぐに注目が集まった。あるゲーム記事では、「原石を削り、宝石を作り、そしてク総を召喚？」という見出しがそのまま使われた。米国のゲームメディア『PC Gamer』の編集者は、実際にプレイした後、宝石をカットするプロセスは「見た目通り満足感がある」と記した。ゲームサイト『BizzNerd』のレビューでは、本作を「ゆったりとしていて風変わり」と評し、来年のシミュレーションゲームにおけるダークホース候補として注目している。
「賭石」は、今日のプレイヤーがこのゲームに対して抱く第一印象だが、最初のプロトタイプには、その片鱗すらなかった。
ランプワームは、「スポットライト」バージョンの様子を振り返る。プレイヤーが原石を購入し、ノミで割ると、システムが不純物率と破損度を計算する。その後のカット工程では画面は何も表示されず、進行バーが動くだけで、それが完了すると決まった宝石のモデルがポップアップ表示される。「ただループするばかりで、深みがまったくなかった」と彼は振り返る。初期バージョンには鑑定という概念すらなかったことも覚えている。「当時は『賭石』さえなかったんだ。」
転機は外部からの視点によってもたらされた。パブリッシャーがプロトタイプを見て、この「賭石」という方向性には「将来性がある」と指摘したのだ。その後、灯蠕虫は購入の段階に鑑定要素を追加した。プレイヤーは道具と経験をもとに原石の品質を判断する必要があり、運も一部を占める。選定、採掘、カット、セッティング、販売――一粒の石をめぐる完全なサイクルがこうして完結し、初めて「賭石」が真の意味で成立するのだ。
原石選び――ゲームの重要な要素の一つ
しかし、このゲームプレイが成立するかどうか、当初「灯蠕虫」には確信がなかった。2025年10月、パブリッシャーの協力のもと、数十人規模の限定テストが実施された。テストのフィードバックは「ポテンシャルはあるが、まだ粗削り」というものだったが、ラン・ワームはそこから必要な確信を得た。「その時に初めて、このゲームプレイは確かに成立すると確信したのです。」
その後、開発のペースは明らかに加速し、2026年6月にはSteamでオープンベータテストが開始され、10月の「新製品フェスティバル」期間中に無料体験版が正式にリリースされました。記事の冒頭で挙げた数字は、これらに基づいています。
このゲームの舞台となるのは、架空の地下都市です。プレイヤーは、行方不明になった姉が残した宝石店「朱紅館」を引き継ぎ、経営を通じて姉の行方に関する手がかりを探していきます。この都市は、「記憶喪失熱」と呼ばれる疫病に覆われており、主要な文明から孤立し、まるで歴史に忘れ去られた一幕のようだ。
ランプワームは、まず「宝石」という媒体を確定し、次にそれにふさわしい文化的属性として「記念と記憶」を見出し、それを足掛かりとして対立を生み出したと語った。「まるで小説家になったかのように振る舞い、この世界に少しばかりの対立を仕掛けたのだ」と。
細部によって、この地下都市が徐々に現実味を帯びてくる。店には客が行き交い、宝石を買う客や原石を売る商人、奇妙な遺物を探し求める男、金貸し、お茶を売る女などがいる。ゲームの設定によれば、評判が高くなればなるほど、訪れる客は奇妙なものになっていく。プレイヤーは経営を通じて「知覚値」と呼ばれる数値を蓄積し、ある閾値を超えると異変が現れ始める。心臓の鼓動が聞こえる部屋、底の見えない穴、雑音に汚染されたラジオの受信チャンネルなどだ。
このゲームのキャッチコピーには、「自らの手で寰茵の皮を剥ぎ取った者は、必ずその身をもって歴史の余波に耐えねばならない」と記されている。
この恐怖の度合いについて、機核網の表現は「顔に飛びかかってくるわけではないが、背筋が凍るほど怖い」と、実に的確に言い当てている。
03
リアリティはゲームプレイに譲歩しなければならない
多くのプレイヤーがこのゲームについて語る際、「プロ級」という言葉を使う。カット、ファセット、セッティングといった専門用語や工程は、一見すると本格的に見える。しかし、ランプワーム本人はこの評価に対して意外な反応を見せた。「本当の宝石職人ってどんなものか、僕にも分からないよ。」
実際のジュエリー制作には、素材選び、宝石のカット・研磨、デザインなど、多くの工程があり、それぞれに専門的なノウハウが存在します。『灯蠕虫』が目指しているのは、これらの工程を結びつけ、プレイヤーに原石からジュエリーが完成するまでの全工程を体験してもらうことです。
取材のために、彼は大量の宝石加工動画を視聴し、教科書も読み込み、「八角手」といったファセット加工の技法やカットの順序について研究した。「灯蠕虫」は他にもカットをテーマにしたゲームをプレイしたことがあるが、教科書通りの方法で少しずつ角度を調整していくやり方は「プレイしていて息苦しい」と感じた。現実を完全に再現したシミュレーションよりも、工程を抽象化した後にどれだけ楽しめるかを重視しているのだ。
ゲームプレイの磨き上げにおいて、『ランプワーム』は、プレイヤーが気づきにくい部分に多大な労力を費やしています。ゲーム内では、加工用の鉱石の一つひとつが1万個近くの微細なユニットで構成されており、それらが互いに作用し合っています。『マインクラフト』のようなボクセルワールドに似ていますが、レンダリングはより滑らかです。『灯蠕虫』の言葉を借りれば、「鉱石の一つひとつが小さな世界なのです」。
石を叩く、トントントン
切断の工程はむしろ単純で、プログラムの観点から見れば単なるモデルのパネルに過ぎませんが、鉱石の加工工程には硬度、靭性、耐酸性など、さまざまな次元の属性が与えられており、熱処理の要素も現在開発中です。灯蠕虫の目標は、すべてのツールに存在意義を持たせることです。彼の構想では、鉱石の加工がプレイヤーの時間の6～7割を占め、切断が1割、残りはアクセサリー製作に充てられることになります。
ここでは、リアリティよりもゲーム性が優先されています。特定の鉱物の特性を設計する際、灯蠕虫は直感に合致することを重視しており、例えばダイヤモンドやコランダムは硬いものであるべきだといった点に重点を置き、現実の物理的パラメータを項目ごとに再現する必要はないと考えています。プレイヤーの間で頻繁に話題に上る「万砕爺」ことリン葉石については、漫画『宝石の国』の影響があり、『灯虫』はこの極めて脆い鉱物をゲーム内で印象深く残したいと考えた。
最大の譲歩は品質システムにおいて行われた。最初のテスト段階では、ゲーム内に品質ランクは存在せず、破損率といった現実的な特性によって宝石の良し悪しが直接定義されていた。その後、開発チームはこの設計の問題点に気づいた。プレイヤーがSNSで成果を共有する際、「完璧な品質の宝石を手に入れた」という表現なら一目で理解できるが、「破損度がゼロの宝石を手に入れた」という表現では、意味が伝わりづらいのだ。
現在、ゲーム内の宝石は「粗悪」「普通」「優良」「卓越」「完璧」の5段階に分類されている。その代償として、時折、破損率が90％にも達する「完璧」品質の宝石が出現することもある。彼はこれが現実的ではないと認めつつも、倉庫に並ぶ色とりどりの品質ラベルがもたらす達成感を拒むプレイヤーはいないだろう。
プレイヤーが「夢中になる」理由は、別のデザイン要素にある。『灯蠕虫』は当初、『漁帆暗涌』のような小規模な作品をモデルにしていたが、賭石メカニズムと品質システムが導入されたことで、収集の深みとリスクの駆け引きが重なり合い、彼はこれを「乗算効果」と表現した。プレイヤーがやめられなくなる状態について、彼の総括は極めて率直だ。「人間の本性の弱点を利用しただけで、特に言うことはない。みんなギャンブルが好きだし、品質の異なるキラキラしたものを集めるのが好きなんだ。」
「小紅書」上のユーザーレビュー
体験版の公開後も、調整は継続して行われています。ゲーム内にはアンケートや不具合報告の窓口が組み込まれており、各テスト終了後には毎回、プレイヤーからの意見を幅広く収集しています。中国のQQグループや海外のDiscordでは、プレイヤーが直接彼に連絡を取ることができます。
記事の最後に、ランプワームは「ゲーム茶館」を通じてプレイヤーに2つのメッセージを伝えてほしいと依頼した。
まず、ゲーム内のホラー要素についてですが、体験プレイ期間中、ゲームの雰囲気のせいでプレイを諦めてしまったプレイヤーもいました。これに対し、灯蠕虫は「低恐怖モード」を実装することを約束しました。このモードでは、巨大な蛾や停電といった特に不気味な出来事を、よりマイルドな表現に調整する予定です。ただし、このモードの実装には複雑なロジックが絡むため、正式版発売時には間に合わない可能性があり、その後できるだけ早く追加する予定です。
恐怖要素を完全に排除することについては、灯蠕虫氏は「難しい」と率直に認めている。例えば、鉱石から生えている目といった要素はゲームプレイと密接に結びついており、これを削除するのは実に惜しいからだ。同時に、ゲームの通常モードでは、突然の驚かせや追跡戦は発生しないため、プレイヤーは安心してプレイできると強調した。
次に、一部のプレイヤーから指摘されためまいの問題についてですが、ランプワーム氏は、この件に関する苦情がホラー要素に関するものよりも多いと述べ、正式版ではテレポート式の高速移動モードを実装することを約束しました。
もちろん、プレイヤーが気にする点はこれら2つだけではありません。例えば、よく話題に上がる経済システムの問題ですが、体験版では、手間をかけて作成したアクセサリーが、原石よりも安く売れてしまうことがありました。これについて「灯蠕虫」は、装飾品の価値は主に「評判」の獲得やステータスボーナスの提供にこそあると説明しています。具体的な数値については今後のバージョンでさらに調整が行われる予定です。また、ゲーム後半で「お金を使い切れない」という問題についても、正式版では解決される見込みです。さらに、まだ開放されていない大量のアップグレード項目、装備、高級ツールも多数存在します。
さらに先を見据えた計画もすでに練られている。錬金術の色彩を帯びたその世界観は、彼が過去のプロジェクトから引き継いだ蓄積によるものであり、『地淵の宝石職人』はその中で「いわば序章」に過ぎない。
html:
この1ヶ月余りの間、小紅書では次々とユーザーが自作のジュエリー作品を投稿し続けている。写真に写る指輪やネックレスには、色や輝きが異なる宝石が散りばめられており、そのデザインは上品なものから奇抜なものまで様々だ。中には、宝石を組み合わせて「巨大な剣」を作り上げた人もいるほどだ。

これらのアクセサリーはすべて、同じゲーム『地淵の宝石職人』から生まれたものです。

このゲームの正式版はまだ発売されていませんが、Steamで公開された無料体験版にはすでに560件以上のユーザーレビューが寄せられており、高評価率は86％で、プラットフォームから「特に好評」と評価されています。また、ウィッシュリスト登録数は17万件に達しています。9月末には、2026年indiePlay中国インディーゲームコンテストの「最優秀デザイン賞」にもノミネートされました。

そして、これらの数字は、たった1人で構成される「開発チーム」によるものだ。

01

まずテンセントで1年間働いた

『地淵の宝石職人』の作者である灯蠕虫は、テンセントでゲーム業界への第一歩を踏み出した。大学卒業後、同社のパブリッシング部門でゲームプランナーとして勤務した。

この経験は1年にも満たなかったが、彼のゲームに対する理解を一変させた。学生時代、灯蠕虫もいくつかのインディーズゲームを制作していたが、当時は自己表現を重視しており、作品が売れるかどうかはあまり気にしていなかった。しかし、パブリッシング業務に携わる中で、彼は初めてプロジェクトの商業的価値について真剣に考えるようになった。

2023年9月、灯蠕虫は退職を決意した。その時点で入社してまだ1年も経っていなかった。彼は、当初の計画ではまず数年働いて資金を貯め、その後インディーズゲームの開発を始めるつもりだったと振り返るが、インディーズ開発にかかる費用は実際には限られていると判断し、予定より早く行動に移した。

退職後、彼が手掛けた最初のプロジェクトは、香水と錬金術をテーマにしたもので、『スルタンのゲーム』や『密教シミュレーター』に近いゲームプレイのカードゲームだった。このプロジェクトは1年余り続いたが、次第に頓挫してしまった。

ランプワームのアトリエ

彼にはインスピレーションを記録する習慣があり、ここ数年、実現可能だと感じ、かつやりたいと思ったアイデアはすべて「ライトワーム」がインスピレーション・データベースに記録し、開発の優先順位に従って並べ替えている。

一部のクリエイティブなテーマは同じ創作コンセプトを共有しており、灯蠕虫はそれを「復魅」と総称している。これは、現実世界において美しく、情緒的な価値はあるものの、実用性のないものをゲームの世界観に取り入れ、そこに実用的な機能を持たせることを意味する。香水を例に挙げると、現実世界の香水、宝石、タトゥーといったものは、人々の美や記憶、アイデンティティに対する想像を宿している一方で、別の視点から見れば、単なる情緒的価値しか持たない「偽物」に過ぎない。しかし彼は、ゲームの中でこうした想像を現実のものにしたいと考えている。香水は単なる香りではなく、人の肉体さえも変え、さらには魂にまで作用し得るものなのだ。

2024年10月、彼はインスピレーションの宝庫から「宝石」というテーマを選び出し、「スポットライト」への参加に向けて『地淵の宝石職人』の最初のバージョンを作成した。

02

まず遊び方を決めてから、物語を作り上げる

体験版が公開されると、すぐに注目が集まった。あるゲーム記事では、「原石を削り、宝石を作り、そしてク総を召喚？」という見出しがそのまま使われた。米国のゲームメディア『PC Gamer』の編集者は、実際にプレイした後、宝石をカットするプロセスは「見た目通り満足感がある」と記した。ゲームサイト『BizzNerd』のレビューでは、本作を「ゆったりとしていて風変わり」と評し、来年のシミュレーションゲームにおけるダークホース候補として注目している。

「賭石」は、今日のプレイヤーがこのゲームに対して抱く第一印象だが、最初のプロトタイプには、その片鱗すらなかった。

ランプワームは、「スポットライト」バージョンの様子を振り返る。プレイヤーが原石を購入し、ノミで割ると、システムが不純物率と破損度を計算する。その後のカット工程では画面は何も表示されず、進行バーが動くだけで、それが完了すると決まった宝石のモデルがポップアップ表示される。「ただループするばかりで、深みがまったくなかった」と彼は振り返る。初期バージョンには鑑定という概念すらなかったことも覚えている。「当時は『賭石』さえなかったんだ。」

転機は外部からの視点によってもたらされた。パブリッシャーがプロトタイプを見て、この「賭石」という方向性には「将来性がある」と指摘したのだ。その後、灯蠕虫は購入の段階に鑑定要素を追加した。プレイヤーは道具と経験をもとに原石の品質を判断する必要があり、運も一部を占める。選定、採掘、カット、セッティング、販売――一粒の石をめぐる完全なサイクルがこうして完結し、初めて「賭石」が真の意味で成立するのだ。

原石選び――ゲームの重要な要素の一つ

しかし、このゲームプレイが成立するかどうか、当初「灯蠕虫」には確信がなかった。2025年10月、パブリッシャーの協力のもと、数十人規模の限定テストが実施された。テストのフィードバックは「ポテンシャルはあるが、まだ粗削り」というものだったが、ラン・ワームはそこから必要な確信を得た。「その時に初めて、このゲームプレイは確かに成立すると確信したのです。」

その後、開発のペースは明らかに加速し、2026年6月にはSteamでオープンベータテストが開始され、10月の「新製品フェスティバル」期間中に無料体験版が正式にリリースされました。記事の冒頭で挙げた数字は、これらに基づいています。

このゲームの舞台となるのは、架空の地下都市です。プレイヤーは、行方不明になった姉が残した宝石店「朱紅館」を引き継ぎ、経営を通じて姉の行方に関する手がかりを探していきます。この都市は、「記憶喪失熱」と呼ばれる疫病に覆われており、主要な文明から孤立し、まるで歴史に忘れ去られた一幕のようだ。

ランプワームは、まず「宝石」という媒体を確定し、次にそれにふさわしい文化的属性として「記念と記憶」を見出し、それを足掛かりとして対立を生み出したと語った。「まるで小説家になったかのように振る舞い、この世界に少しばかりの対立を仕掛けたのだ」と。

細部によって、この地下都市が徐々に現実味を帯びてくる。店には客が行き交い、宝石を買う客や原石を売る商人、奇妙な遺物を探し求める男、金貸し、お茶を売る女などがいる。ゲームの設定によれば、評判が高くなればなるほど、訪れる客は奇妙なものになっていく。プレイヤーは経営を通じて「知覚値」と呼ばれる数値を蓄積し、ある閾値を超えると異変が現れ始める。心臓の鼓動が聞こえる部屋、底の見えない穴、雑音に汚染されたラジオの受信チャンネルなどだ。

このゲームのキャッチコピーには、「自らの手で寰茵の皮を剥ぎ取った者は、必ずその身をもって歴史の余波に耐えねばならない」と記されている。

この恐怖の度合いについて、機核網の表現は「顔に飛びかかってくるわけではないが、背筋が凍るほど怖い」と、実に的確に言い当てている。

03

リアリティはゲームプレイに譲歩しなければならない

多くのプレイヤーがこのゲームについて語る際、「プロ級」という言葉を使う。カット、ファセット、セッティングといった専門用語や工程は、一見すると本格的に見える。しかし、ランプワーム本人はこの評価に対して意外な反応を見せた。「本当の宝石職人ってどんなものか、僕にも分からないよ。」

実際のジュエリー制作には、素材選び、宝石のカット・研磨、デザインなど、多くの工程があり、それぞれに専門的なノウハウが存在します。『灯蠕虫』が目指しているのは、これらの工程を結びつけ、プレイヤーに原石からジュエリーが完成するまでの全工程を体験してもらうことです。

取材のために、彼は大量の宝石加工動画を視聴し、教科書も読み込み、「八角手」といったファセット加工の技法やカットの順序について研究した。「灯蠕虫」は他にもカットをテーマにしたゲームをプレイしたことがあるが、教科書通りの方法で少しずつ角度を調整していくやり方は「プレイしていて息苦しい」と感じた。現実を完全に再現したシミュレーションよりも、工程を抽象化した後にどれだけ楽しめるかを重視しているのだ。

ゲームプレイの磨き上げにおいて、『ランプワーム』は、プレイヤーが気づきにくい部分に多大な労力を費やしています。ゲーム内では、加工用の鉱石の一つひとつが1万個近くの微細なユニットで構成されており、それらが互いに作用し合っています。『マインクラフト』のようなボクセルワールドに似ていますが、レンダリングはより滑らかです。『灯蠕虫』の言葉を借りれば、「鉱石の一つひとつが小さな世界なのです」。

石を叩く、トントントン

切断の工程はむしろ単純で、プログラムの観点から見れば単なるモデルのパネルに過ぎませんが、鉱石の加工工程には硬度、靭性、耐酸性など、さまざまな次元の属性が与えられており、熱処理の要素も現在開発中です。灯蠕虫の目標は、すべてのツールに存在意義を持たせることです。彼の構想では、鉱石の加工がプレイヤーの時間の6～7割を占め、切断が1割、残りはアクセサリー製作に充てられることになります。

ここでは、リアリティよりもゲーム性が優先されています。特定の鉱物の特性を設計する際、灯蠕虫は直感に合致することを重視しており、例えばダイヤモンドやコランダムは硬いものであるべきだといった点に重点を置き、現実の物理的パラメータを項目ごとに再現する必要はないと考えています。プレイヤーの間で頻繁に話題に上る「万砕爺」ことリン葉石については、漫画『宝石の国』の影響があり、『灯虫』はこの極めて脆い鉱物をゲーム内で印象深く残したいと考えた。

最大の譲歩は品質システムにおいて行われた。最初のテスト段階では、ゲーム内に品質ランクは存在せず、破損率といった現実的な特性によって宝石の良し悪しが直接定義されていた。その後、開発チームはこの設計の問題点に気づいた。プレイヤーがSNSで成果を共有する際、「完璧な品質の宝石を手に入れた」という表現なら一目で理解できるが、「破損度がゼロの宝石を手に入れた」という表現では、意味が伝わりづらいのだ。

現在、ゲーム内の宝石は「粗悪」「普通」「優良」「卓越」「完璧」の5段階に分類されている。その代償として、時折、破損率が90％にも達する「完璧」品質の宝石が出現することもある。彼はこれが現実的ではないと認めつつも、倉庫に並ぶ色とりどりの品質ラベルがもたらす達成感を拒むプレイヤーはいないだろう。

プレイヤーが「夢中になる」理由は、別のデザイン要素にある。『灯蠕虫』は当初、『漁帆暗涌』のような小規模な作品をモデルにしていたが、賭石メカニズムと品質システムが導入されたことで、収集の深みとリスクの駆け引きが重なり合い、彼はこれを「乗算効果」と表現した。プレイヤーがやめられなくなる状態について、彼の総括は極めて率直だ。「人間の本性の弱点を利用しただけで、特に言うことはない。みんなギャンブルが好きだし、品質の異なるキラキラしたものを集めるのが好きなんだ。」

「小紅書」上のユーザーレビュー

体験版の公開後も、調整は継続して行われています。ゲーム内にはアンケートや不具合報告の窓口が組み込まれており、各テスト終了後には毎回、プレイヤーからの意見を幅広く収集しています。中国のQQグループや海外のDiscordでは、プレイヤーが直接彼に連絡を取ることができます。

記事の最後に、ランプワームは「ゲーム茶館」を通じてプレイヤーに2つのメッセージを伝えてほしいと依頼した。

まず、ゲーム内のホラー要素についてですが、体験プレイ期間中、ゲームの雰囲気のせいでプレイを諦めてしまったプレイヤーもいました。これに対し、灯蠕虫は「低恐怖モード」を実装することを約束しました。このモードでは、巨大な蛾や停電といった特に不気味な出来事を、よりマイルドな表現に調整する予定です。ただし、このモードの実装には複雑なロジックが絡むため、正式版発売時には間に合わない可能性があり、その後できるだけ早く追加する予定です。

恐怖要素を完全に排除することについては、灯蠕虫氏は「難しい」と率直に認めている。例えば、鉱石から生えている目といった要素はゲームプレイと密接に結びついており、これを削除するのは実に惜しいからだ。同時に、ゲームの通常モードでは、突然の驚かせや追跡戦は発生しないため、プレイヤーは安心してプレイできると強調した。

次に、一部のプレイヤーから指摘されためまいの問題についてですが、ランプワーム氏は、この件に関する苦情がホラー要素に関するものよりも多いと述べ、正式版ではテレポート式の高速移動モードを実装することを約束しました。

もちろん、プレイヤーが気にする点はこれら2つだけではありません。例えば、よく話題に上がる経済システムの問題ですが、体験版では、手間をかけて作成したアクセサリーが、原石よりも安く売れてしまうことがありました。これについて「灯蠕虫」は、装飾品の価値は主に「評判」の獲得やステータスボーナスの提供にこそあると説明しています。具体的な数値については今後のバージョンでさらに調整が行われる予定です。また、ゲーム後半で「お金を使い切れない」という問題についても、正式版では解決される見込みです。さらに、まだ開放されていない大量のアップグレード項目、装備、高級ツールも多数存在します。

さらに先を見据えた計画もすでに練られている。錬金術の色彩を帯びたその世界観は、彼が過去のプロジェクトから引き継いだ蓄積によるものであり、『地淵の宝石職人』はその中で「いわば序章」に過ぎない。

title: With 170,000 items on its wish list, another under-the-radar dark horse has emerged among domestic indie games.
text:
Over the past month or so, people on Xiaohongshu have been constantly sharing photos of their jewelry creations. The rings and necklaces in the photos are set with gemstones of various colors, and their designs range from elegant to quirky; some people have even used gemstones to craft a “giant sword.”
All of these accessories are from the same game, *The Abyss Jeweler*.
The full version of this game has not yet been released, but its free demo on Steam has already garnered over 560 player reviews, with an 86% approval rating; it has been labeled “Overwhelmingly Positive” by the platform and has 170,000 wishlist entries.In late September, it was also nominated for the “Best Design” award at the 2026 indiePlay China Independent Game Competition.
And these figures come from a “development team” consisting of just one person.
01
I worked at Tencent for a year first
Deng Runchong, the author of *The Jeweler of the Abyss*, took his first step into the gaming industry at Tencent. After graduating from college, he worked there as a game designer on the publishing team.
This experience lasted less than a year, but it changed his understanding of games. As a student, Deng Worm had also created some indie games, approaching them more as a form of self-expression and not worrying too much about whether they would sell. The training he received at the publishing studio prompted him to seriously consider the commercial value of a project for the first time.
In September 2023, Lampworm decided to quit his job; he had been there for less than a year. He recalls that his original plan was to work for a few years, save up enough money, and then start developing indie games, but after realizing that the costs of independent development were actually quite limited, he decided to take the plunge sooner than expected.
The first project he worked on after leaving his job was a card game themed around perfume and alchemy, with gameplay similar to *The Sultan’s Game* and *Esoteric Simulator*. He worked on the project for a little over a year, but it gradually fell apart.
The Lampworm Studio
He has a habit of jotting down his ideas. Over the past few years, whenever he’s come across an idea he felt he could—and wanted to—pursue, Lampworm has added it to his idea bank and queued it up according to development priority.
Some creative themes share the same conceptual framework, which Lightworm summarizes as “re-enchantment”—that is, taking things from reality that are beautiful and emotionally meaningful but serve no practical purpose, and incorporating them into the game’s world to give them a practical function.Take perfume as an example: in reality, objects such as perfume, gemstones, and tattoos carry people’s imaginings of beauty, memory, and identity, yet from another perspective, they are merely pseudo-objects with only emotional value. He wants to make these imaginings a reality within the game. Perfume is not just a scent; it can also alter a person’s flesh and blood, and even affect the soul.
In October 2024, he drew on the theme of “gemstones” from his inspiration library and created the first version of *The Jeweler of the Abyss* for the Spotlight competition.
02
First, decide on the gameplay; then, create the story.
After the demo was released, it quickly garnered attention. One gaming article used the headline “Cut jade, craft jewelry, and then summon Ke Zong?” After trying it out, an editor from the U.S. gaming media outlet PC Gamer wrote that the gem-cutting process was “as satisfying as it looks,”A review on the gaming website BizzNerd described it as “slow and quirky” and touted it as a potential dark horse among next year’s simulation games.
“Jade Gambling” is the first impression players have of this game today, but it wasn’t even a glimmer of an idea in the original prototype.
Lampworm recalls what the “Spotlight” version looked like: players would purchase rough stones, use a chisel to split them open, and the system would calculate the impurity rate and damage level. The subsequent cutting process was shown with no visuals—only a progress bar that moved across the screen—and once it reached the end, a pre-determined gem model would pop up.“It was just an empty loop with no depth at all,” he recalls, noting that the original version didn’t even include an appraisal feature. “Back then, there wasn’t even a ‘gambling on rough stones’ mechanic.”
The turning point came from an outside perspective: after the publisher reviewed the prototype, they suggested that the “gambling on jade” concept “had potential.”Lampworm subsequently added an appraisal mechanic to the purchasing phase, requiring players to use tools and experience to assess the quality of the rough stones—though luck also plays a part. From selection to quarrying, cutting, setting, and selling, the complete cycle surrounding a single stone is thus closed, and the “gambling on jade” concept truly comes to life.
Selecting Rough Stones: A Key Part of the Game
However, at first, Lightworm wasn’t sure if the gameplay concept would work.In October 2025, with the publisher’s assistance, the game underwent a small-scale test involving several dozen participants. The feedback was that it had “potential, but was rough around the edges,” and Lampworm gained the confirmation they needed from this: “That’s when I truly became convinced that this gameplay concept was actually viable.”
Development subsequently picked up significantly. In June 2026, the game entered open beta on Steam, and in October, during the New Releases Festival, a free demo was officially released. The figures mentioned at the beginning of this article come from these events.
The setting for this game is a fictional underground city, where players inherit the jewelry store “Vermilion Hall” left behind by their missing older sister and search for clues to her disappearance while running the business.This city is currently gripped by an epidemic known as “Amnesia Fever.” Isolated from the wider civilization, it feels like an interlude forgotten by history.
The Lampworm said that he first settled on the gemstone as his medium, then sought out cultural attributes for it—specifically, commemoration and memory—and used these as an anchor to create conflict: “I pretended to be a novelist and created some conflict in this world.”
The details gradually bring this underground city to life: customers come and go—some buying gems, others selling rough stones, as well as men searching for strange relics, moneylenders, and women selling tea.According to the game’s mechanics, the higher your reputation, the stranger the customers who walk through your door. As you manage your business, you’ll accumulate a stat called “Awareness.” Once you cross a certain threshold, strange phenomena begin to occur: rooms where you can hear heartbeats, bottomless pits, and contaminated radio channels.
The game’s tagline reads, “Whoever peels away the shell of the world with their own hands will inevitably bear the aftershocks of history.”
Jike.cn’s description of the horror’s intensity is quite accurate: “It doesn’t jump out at you, but it still sends shivers down your spine.”
03
Realism Must Give Way to Gameplay
Many players describe this game as “professional”—with terms like “cutting,” “faceting,” and “setting,” the terminology and processes seem quite authentic. Lampworm’s reaction to this assessment was somewhat unexpected: “I don’t even know what a real jeweler is.”
In the real world, jewelry making involves multiple stages—including material selection, gemstone cutting and polishing, and design—each with its own specialized techniques. What “Lampworm” aims to do is connect these stages, allowing players to experience the entire process from a rough stone to a finished piece of jewelry.
To gather material, he watched countless videos on jewelry crafting, pored over textbooks, and studied techniques and cutting sequences for faceting styles like the octagonal hand cut.Lampworm has also experimented with games featuring other cutting themes, but he found the textbook method of adjusting angles bit by bit to be “a real drag.” Rather than a simulation that perfectly replicates reality, he places greater value on whether these abstracted processes are fun to play with.
When it comes to refining the gameplay, a significant portion of the effort put into *Lightworm* went into areas that players might not easily notice.Every piece of ore used for processing in the game is composed of nearly 10,000 minute units that interact with one another, creating a voxel-based world similar to *Minecraft*, only rendered more smoothly. Over the past month or so, people on Xiaohongshu have been constantly sharing photos of their jewelry creations. The rings and necklaces in the photos are set with gemstones of various colors, and their designs range from elegant to quirky; some people have even used gemstones to craft a “giant sword.”

All of these accessories are from the same game, *The Abyss Jeweler*.

The full version of this game has not yet been released, but its free demo on Steam has already garnered over 560 player reviews, with an 86% approval rating; it has been labeled “Overwhelmingly Positive” by the platform and has 170,000 wishlist entries.In late September, it was also nominated for the “Best Design” award at the 2026 indiePlay China Independent Game Competition.

And these figures come from a “development team” consisting of just one person.

01

I worked at Tencent for a year first

Deng Runchong, the author of *The Jeweler of the Abyss*, took his first step into the gaming industry at Tencent. After graduating from college, he worked there as a game designer on the publishing team.

This experience lasted less than a year, but it changed his understanding of games. As a student, Deng Worm had also created some indie games, approaching them more as a form of self-expression and not worrying too much about whether they would sell. The training he received at the publishing studio prompted him to seriously consider the commercial value of a project for the first time.

In September 2023, Lampworm decided to quit his job; he had been there for less than a year. He recalls that his original plan was to work for a few years, save up enough money, and then start developing indie games, but after realizing that the costs of independent development were actually quite limited, he decided to take the plunge sooner than expected.

The first project he worked on after leaving his job was a card game themed around perfume and alchemy, with gameplay similar to *The Sultan’s Game* and *Esoteric Simulator*. He worked on the project for a little over a year, but it gradually fell apart.

The Lampworm Studio

He has a habit of jotting down his ideas. Over the past few years, whenever he’s come across an idea he felt he could—and wanted to—pursue, Lampworm has added it to his idea bank and queued it up according to development priority.

Some creative themes share the same conceptual framework, which Lightworm summarizes as “re-enchantment”—that is, taking things from reality that are beautiful and emotionally meaningful but serve no practical purpose, and incorporating them into the game’s world to give them a practical function.Take perfume as an example: in reality, objects such as perfume, gemstones, and tattoos carry people’s imaginings of beauty, memory, and identity, yet from another perspective, they are merely pseudo-objects with only emotional value. He wants to make these imaginings a reality within the game. Perfume is not just a scent; it can also alter a person’s flesh and blood, and even affect the soul.

In October 2024, he drew on the theme of “gemstones” from his inspiration library and created the first version of *The Jeweler of the Abyss* for the Spotlight competition.

02

First, decide on the gameplay; then, create the story.

After the demo was released, it quickly garnered attention. One gaming article used the headline “Cut jade, craft jewelry, and then summon Ke Zong?” After trying it out, an editor from the U.S. gaming media outlet PC Gamer wrote that the gem-cutting process was “as satisfying as it looks,”A review on the gaming website BizzNerd described it as “slow and quirky” and touted it as a potential dark horse among next year’s simulation games.

“Jade Gambling” is the first impression players have of this game today, but it wasn’t even a glimmer of an idea in the original prototype.

Lampworm recalls what the “Spotlight” version looked like: players would purchase rough stones, use a chisel to split them open, and the system would calculate the impurity rate and damage level. The subsequent cutting process was shown with no visuals—only a progress bar that moved across the screen—and once it reached the end, a pre-determined gem model would pop up.“It was just an empty loop with no depth at all,” he recalls, noting that the original version didn’t even include an appraisal feature. “Back then, there wasn’t even a ‘gambling on rough stones’ mechanic.”

The turning point came from an outside perspective: after the publisher reviewed the prototype, they suggested that the “gambling on jade” concept “had potential.”Lampworm subsequently added an appraisal mechanic to the purchasing phase, requiring players to use tools and experience to assess the quality of the rough stones—though luck also plays a part. From selection to quarrying, cutting, setting, and selling, the complete cycle surrounding a single stone is thus closed, and the “gambling on jade” concept truly comes to life.

Selecting Rough Stones: A Key Part of the Game

However, at first, Lightworm wasn’t sure if the gameplay concept would work.In October 2025, with the publisher’s assistance, the game underwent a small-scale test involving several dozen participants. The feedback was that it had “potential, but was rough around the edges,” and Lampworm gained the confirmation they needed from this: “That’s when I truly became convinced that this gameplay concept was actually viable.”

Development subsequently picked up significantly. In June 2026, the game entered open beta on Steam, and in October, during the New Releases Festival, a free demo was officially released. The figures mentioned at the beginning of this article come from these events.

The setting for this game is a fictional underground city, where players inherit the jewelry store “Vermilion Hall” left behind by their missing older sister and search for clues to her disappearance while running the business.This city is currently gripped by an epidemic known as “Amnesia Fever.” Isolated from the wider civilization, it feels like an interlude forgotten by history.

The Lampworm said that he first settled on the gemstone as his medium, then sought out cultural attributes for it—specifically, commemoration and memory—and used these as an anchor to create conflict: “I pretended to be a novelist and created some conflict in this world.”

The details gradually bring this underground city to life: customers come and go—some buying gems, others selling rough stones, as well as men searching for strange relics, moneylenders, and women selling tea.According to the game’s mechanics, the higher your reputation, the stranger the customers who walk through your door. As you manage your business, you’ll accumulate a stat called “Awareness.” Once you cross a certain threshold, strange phenomena begin to occur: rooms where you can hear heartbeats, bottomless pits, and contaminated radio channels.

The game’s tagline reads, “Whoever peels away the shell of the world with their own hands will inevitably bear the aftershocks of history.”

Jike.cn’s description of the horror’s intensity is quite accurate: “It doesn’t jump out at you, but it still sends shivers down your spine.”

03

Many players describe this game as “professional”—with terms like “cutting,” “faceting,” and “setting,” the terminology and processes seem quite authentic. Lampworm’s reaction to this assessment was somewhat unexpected: “I don’t even know what a real jeweler is.”

In the real world, jewelry making involves multiple stages—including material selection, gemstone cutting and polishing, and design—each with its own specialized techniques. What “Lampworm” aims to do is connect these stages, allowing players to experience the entire process from a rough stone to a finished piece of jewelry.

title: A Conversation with the Creators Behind “Operation Delta”: Industrial Ambition and Answers Amid a Tidal Wave
text:
Have you ever watched a disaster movie? When I was playing the new season of *Operation Delta*—which had been upgraded to UE5—and looked up to see massive waves dozens of meters high crashing down on Skyport, I understood why this genre has remained so enduring in film history.
As the guided missile that sealed the victory struck, a massive explosion first echoed throughout the harbor, followed immediately by a surging tidal wave that crashed into roads, bridges, and buildings, sending up vast plumes of white spray.As the wave drew near, its destructive power became all the more apparent: it smashed buildings in its path, sweeping up vehicles, trees, streetlights, and large chunks of reinforced concrete debris—and G.T.I. operatives who hadn’t managed to take cover in a safe zone were swept away along with everything else.
Bitch
It’s hard not to be reminded of the scene in the movie *The Day After Tomorrow* where floodwaters engulf New York—an irresistible force steadily closing in, the familiar world suddenly thrown into chaos, and the audience left to witness the unparalleled power of nature.
Players also love this sense of tension. Many gamers with high-end PCs have recorded the entire sequence of the “Giant Wave” event at maximum 4K settings and shared the footage online. Especially after the Sky Harbor map was upgraded with UE5 technology, Unreal Engine 5 features like Nanite and Lumen have made the sight of the giant wave crashing into the city look incredibly realistic.“My graphics card is about to catch fire!” is the most common comment under these videos; others joke, “This is the wave Delta has been waiting for his whole life.”
Even in overseas comment sections, quite a few players have been comparing Delta’s gameplay footage to blockbusters like *Battlefield*, and their comments are full of love.
For a long time, we’ve taken for granted the dominance of overseas AAA titles in terms of physical destruction and lighting effects, praising *Call of Duty* for its lighting details and *Battlefield* for its environmental destruction—yet it remains rare for domestic FPS games to receive similar recognition.
This may mean that, at long last, a Chinese-developed FPS game has, through its top-notch performance, broken into the technical arena where overseas FPS games have long held a leading position.
So how did *Operation Delta*, which has been live for two years, pull this off?With this question in mind, I spoke with the lead designer of the “Operation Delta” Comprehensive Battlefield Skyport map, a technical artist, and the head of the engine team. Through their accounts, I saw three distinct aspects: a solid technical foundation, the tenacity to tackle seemingly impossible challenges, and a creator’s heart that remains steadfastly focused on the player experience.
01
Putting an Elephant in a Refrigerator
“The whole process is like putting an elephant in a refrigerator—it’s an epic challenge,” the lead designer at Skyport told me.
The essence of huge waves is water, and simulating water has always been difficult—this is a consensus within the game development industry. Mathematical modeling of waveforms, the sorting of reflections, refractions, and transparent objects; plus water bodies of different locations and types, each with its own color, turbidity, and flow state—each of these requires extremely complex algorithms to implement.Furthermore, according to technical artists, rendering realistic water in a film or TV scene can take dozens of hours to compute a single shot, whereas in a multiplayer FPS, there are only a few milliseconds available for rendering.
Not to mention, in Delta, characters can dive, swim, and operate boats—which requires consideration of the interactions between the water environment, vehicles, and operator skills, as well as ensuring server synchronization in multiplayer mode. Achieving this level of interactivity has already required a tremendous amount of R&D effort.Scale this aquatic environment up a thousand or even ten thousand times, and both the technical difficulty and performance demands skyrocket exponentially. Even when looking at the global multiplayer FPS landscape, they can find almost no direct precedents to draw upon.
“At the first meeting, everyone gasped—‘How could you design something this difficult?’” recalled the technical art specialist, but he quickly added, “Everyone said it was hard, but they were actually really looking forward to bringing it to life.”After all, the idea of “creating waves” at Skyport was so perfectly fitting—it would serve as the emotional catharsis for this epic battle between G.T.I. and Hafke Sky City.
After several rounds of internal discussions, the project team decided to adopt a phased delivery plan: first, they would build a minimum viable demo capable of showcasing the “giant wave” effect to confirm that it could run in its basic form on both PC and mobile platforms; then, they would break down the required artistic details and interactive effects into separate components, implementing them layer by layer and building upon each other.
Multiple teams—including Art, 3C, Technical Art, Design and Engine, Visual Effects, and Performance—were all mobilized.During this period, the technical artists were busy becoming “giant wave experts”—they extensively reviewed academic papers on tsunamis and mathematical modeling of ocean water, and also referenced the fluid dynamics depictions in films such as *2012* and *Haeyundae*, all in pursuit of a single answer:How can we use algorithms to model this ever-changing body of water created by the massive waves?
“Tsunamis in nature are completely different from still water: when they first form, they start as an extremely slow wave, then the wave continues to expand and energy builds up layer by layer until it crashes head-on into the shore, at which point it slows down in certain areas.” A technical art specialist gave an example. They recreated these morphological changes in the game, so players can see them more clearly when looking down from an airplane as the giant wave approaches.
There were also some water effects featuring massive waves that we had to abandon after testing because it was nearly impossible to avoid this long-standing optimization challenge—the massive waves themselves are rendered as full-screen water effects, and when combined with scene fragmentation, splashes, water mist, and skill effects, along with dozens of players and vehicles on the same screen, how could we possibly reduce the performance overhead?
A technical art specialist told me, “There’s no silver bullet for optimization”—every department has to fine-tune the details bit by bit.Specifically for water rendering, they developed a GPU-based software subdivision solution: increasing the mesh density of water in the foreground, reducing it in real time in the background, and precisely removing meshes that players cannot see—all to minimize the rendering overhead for every frame as much as possible.
The final result is that the overall shape of the giant wave is driven by specialized algorithms and curves, with Gerstner waves superimposed on the wave body to add detail to the undulations. As the giant wave advances, the overall color of the water deepens and its turbidity increases, causing this stretch of water to constantly change over time.
These details—which players might inadvertently overlook—combine with a smooth gaming environment to shape the ultimate experience——In real life, people rarely have the chance to face massive waves head-on, but in the game, they can take on the role of a G.T.I. agent and personally experience this overwhelming sense of pressure coming from all directions, allowing the tension that has built up throughout the entire battle to be released all at once in that moment.
02
Amid the Waves
At this point, the wave’s structure has taken shape. But the project is only halfway complete. The other half involves taking the concept a step further. “We don’t just want to create the water itself and make it look better; we also want to build a series of interactions around it to make the threat posed by the giant wave feel more believable to players.”
Fortunately, they’ve accumulated a wide range of visual techniques over the years. For example, from last year’s “Eye of the Storm” map to this year’s “Aftershock” map, Delta has developed a suite of techniques ranging from all-terrain tactical destruction to large-scale building destruction—techniques that are perfectly suited to showcasing the destructive power of giant waves.
One clever touch is that, just as the wave is about to reach the player’s location,the G.T.I. landing craft is swept up by the wave and crashes violently into a building where the player had just been engaged in fierce combat—instantly bringing the sheer power of the wave to life while also adding a sense of G.T.I.’s “do-or-die” situation.
The planners then broke down the scripted events into three acts—before, during, and after the giant wave strikes—and assigned them to various modules such as visuals, audio, and UI. Before the wave hits, the wind swirls violently, flocks of crows take flight in panic, and air-raid sirens blare from all directions.The dynamic weather changes accordingly, and the HUD inside the visor suffers from electromagnetic interference. In the distance, billboards and vegetation have been torn up; water sprays into the air, and a wall of mist sweeps toward the viewer, fully capturing the atmosphere of “a storm is brewing.”
At the same time, they must also consider another issue—continuity and synchronization. In other words, this major event must unfold continuously; players must experience a “what you see is what you get” experience—from where the main wave advances to when operators are hit, and when vehicles and the environment respond. Everyone should also be able to remain actively engaged in the major event at all times.
For example, quite a few players felt after trying it out that “G.T.I. Superman” was a bit over-the-top—when an operator is knocked down by a giant wave, they don’t leave the screen immediately but instead enter an 8-second hit animation, making it look as if they’re “taking the brunt of the wave with their own body.”However, a technical art specialist told me, “If we followed real-world logic—where a giant wave instantly eliminates a player, who is then redeployed—it would actually be a hundred times easier to implement.”
He gave a few examples: “Suppose the player’s screen shows that a massive wave is still far away, but the server determines that the player has already been swept up by it—the sense of immersion is instantly shattered. Or suppose the position of a player jet-skiing or driving a boat in the water isn’t detected correctly, causing the water to appear to pass through the model.”If players were forced to remain in a death animation or a pre-rendered cutscene, none of these issues would need to be addressed. After numerous discussions with the combat engineering team, they ultimately chose the more resource-intensive solution: allowing players to witness the entire event in real time.
The team chose the path with the steepest technical challenge and developed a solution called “Water Tsunami,” which separates the system into a logic layer and a rendering layer: a deterministic function driven by server time “t” ensures millisecond-level synchronization of the giant wave state across the server CPU, client CPU, and GPU, which is then used to render the main wave body and generate interactive feedback.At the same time, they used their in-house water simulation tool, Water ACT, to pre-compute data describing the water environment, enabling them to determine as accurately as possible when players were on the surface, when they were underwater, and when they should switch between different states such as swimming or diving.
Many of the game’s most breathtaking in-game highlights stem from this kind of “grind.” Real-time participation opens up even more possibilities for gameplay—some players use the Silverwing Agent to release a falcon from the top of a skyscraper and watch it soar over the towering waves; others hop into an amphibious vehicle to enjoy the sensation of sinking to the bottom and then resurfacing;some do absolutely nothing, simply savoring the sensation of being knocked over by the waves; and we’ve even seen players posting videos specifically to promote this “must-try activity” at Skyport: hopping on a jet ski and riding the crest of the waves at their peak.
Especially when you enable the “Realistic Mode” graphics option—which utilizes UE5 features—the details of the wave, the city’s lighting and shadows, and the interactions unfolding before your eyes all blend together, allowing everyone to experience a unique “giant wave crashing” sequence from their own perspective.
After listening to the R&D team describe these efforts, I realized that no matter how deeply the discussion delved into technical details, it always came back to the same thing: the player experience.
As the massive wave sweeps through, players find themselves on what feels like a brand-new battlefield, surrounded by rubble and ruins.The two outposts where fierce battles had raged earlier were closed off after being struck by the massive wave, and the new outpost was relocated to the rooftop of a skyscraper. Both sides entered a confrontation with unlimited troops, and the attacking side could even deploy forces from the air. The entire battle shifted from a ground-based advance to vertical attacks and defenses between skyscrapers, completely rewriting the dynamics of the battlefield.
So, what exactly did this massive wave bring to the Delta? It not only allowed players to experience a visual spectacle firsthand, but also transformed that sensory impact into a new combat experience.After the game ends, the slogan “Capture the South Bank” displayed on the screen hints at entirely new possibilities for future battles in Skyport. The giant wave has thus become a tangible, massive variable within the tactical landscape.
03
The more difficult the journey, the more wondrous the sights.
Looking back on the entire R&D process, it’s quite moving.Behind a map event lasting just a few minutes lies the close collaboration and repeated iterations of multiple departments within the Delta team, who overcame a series of technical challenges. As the game enters its long-term operation phase, many teams opt for a “play it safe” approach—doing less to minimize mistakes. So why did TiMi J3 choose to take on such a difficult task?
“Looking back, it seems as though the team has been constantly reaching new heights in user experience, but in reality, the groundwork for many of these seemingly unattainable goals was laid long ago during previous R&D efforts,” the head of the engine team told me.
This statement also reveals a core strategic barrier for the team: technological compounding. Juwang is a prime example: as longtime Delta players know, there is actually a subtle, underlying thread of aquatic research and development running through it.
For example, over the first four seasons, the team studied aquatic ecology during the early stages of development. They gradually figured out how to create “visually appealing water” and explored ways to use technology to describe the physical properties of water, such as color, turbidity, and refraction. In the vast bodies of water in Longbow Valley and Dam Zero, they created visual differences between various areas.
Starting with S5, Delta officially introduced diving and swimming mechanics, evolving from “visually appealing water” to “interactive water.” It was also at this stage that the team began maintaining Water ACT, its in-house water pipeline toolchain, which integrates processes such as water area creation, data generation, configuration, and verification, enabling designers and artists to validate their ideas more quickly.Since then, the team has continued to add new features to the toolchain based on the needs of each season’s updates. For example, the pre-calculated water data used in this “Giant Waves” update to bridge the gap between rendering and gameplay validation was also generated by this toolchain.
As early as 2024, the Delta team took the stage at GDC to share their production pipeline with developers around the world.
Behind the scenes, a dedicated engine team quietly supports the entire R&D system.The head of the engine team told me that, in addition to the water system, they’ve also made customizations to terrain, lighting, the open world, PCG, materials, vegetation, the rendering pipeline, and various compatibility adjustments—they’ve even overhauled streaming and serialization. These deep, low-level “modifications” underpin the implementation of Delta’s various features.
Now, they have officially integrated UE5 capabilities such as Nanite, Lumen, and VSM into Delta, their deeply customized, in-house production pipeline. While maintaining version releases, they are simultaneously elevating the underlying technical foundation. In terms of performance optimization, they spent a month making drastic, custom modifications—from high-level features down to low-level multithreading scheduling—and deployed tens of thousands of lines of code, boosting the game’s base frame rate on the same graphics card from 70–80 frames per second to over 120 frames per second(UE5’s official target is 60 fps)—this was a “hard requirement” set by Producer Shadow.
When the Delta team presented some of their work at this year’s Unreal Fest, a colleague privately told our reporter that what they were doing was “hard to imagine.”
Second, the drive to continuously create great gaming experiences for players is what motivates the team to keep tackling tough challenges. With every technological advancement, we must ask the same question: What new experiences will this bring to players?
Let’s use the “water” theme as an example again. Delta’s exploration of “water” not only leaves a clear trail but also tends to change players’ tactical decisions and gaming experience every season. That’s quite unusual.
For example, when Tidal Prison was introduced in Season 5, the lack of underwater escape routes inevitably left a gap in the narrative experience of a prison break; after the Space 2.0 update, a series of new playstyles—such as the “Buoyancy Ghost” strategy—began to emerge, altering the original dynamics of offense and defense.Then there’s the water system overhaul in Longbow Valley during Season 11, which not only allowed players to enjoy the thrill of high-speed boat races throughout the valley but also sparked a “fishing craze” across the entire map, bringing millions of “anglers” to the Delta overnight…These updates centered around waterways have repeatedly expanded the game’s playability while also influencing players’ specific tactical choices time and again.
The completely revamped Longbow Valley map for Season 11
In Skyport, the success of this major event was largely due to the convergence of two technical advancements: the evolution of water systems and the building destruction mechanics developed through maps like “Aftershock.” Challenges that had previously been tackled separately came together in this update, combining to create a new kind of experience. This is the power of technological compounding.
04
Never Stop Moving
Looking at the trajectory of technology development, we can see that Delta is expanding upon some of the inherent expectations associated with FPS games.
For example, in the past, people used to say that FPS games come down to the fundamentals of game development—games that excel in 3C, gameplay mechanics, and character design are the ones that stand out.But now, when people talk about Delta’s seasonal updates, they’re more interested in what major in-game events are coming, whether the map’s ecosystem will become even richer, and if new Easter eggs and gameplay features will be added. This is a competition on a higher level.
In discussions about AAA games in recent years, “gameplay innovation” and “graphics competition” have often been pitted against each other. But with Delta, we see a completely different picture.Every fundamental technical challenge they’ve overcome in the past—along with the technologies, tools, and experience gained along the way—has equipped them to tackle even more complex ideas. The next update might introduce yet another disruptive gameplay option, enabling the game to continuously create unforgettable and unique experiences for players.
The future will continue to evolve along this path. For example, Delta will explore even more unrestricted “search, engage, and withdraw” gameplay narratives in the upcoming “Valkyrie” map; it will also upgrade more large-scale battlefield maps to UE5. These plans, already on the horizon and poised to launch, offer a glimpse into the potential for Delta’s next leap in gameplay.
People often say that Delta is an outlier in the FPS market in recent years. It has raised the bar for the domestic FPS experience, achieved exceptional commercial success, and is even gradually venturing into uncharted territory—a sector previously dominated by overseas FPS titles.Perhaps this is precisely why: as this massive wave surges past us, its ever-rising tide will continue to propel the game even further.

Have you ever watched a disaster movie? When I was playing the new season of *Operation Delta*—which had been upgraded to UE5—and looked up to see massive waves dozens of meters high crashing down on Skyport, I understood why this genre has remained so enduring in film history.

As the guided missile that sealed the victory struck, a massive explosion first echoed throughout the harbor, followed immediately by a surging tidal wave that crashed into roads, bridges, and buildings, sending up vast plumes of white spray.As the wave drew near, its destructive power became all the more apparent: it smashed buildings in its path, sweeping up vehicles, trees, streetlights, and large chunks of reinforced concrete debris—and G.T.I. operatives who hadn’t managed to take cover in a safe zone were swept away along with everything else.

Bitch

It’s hard not to be reminded of the scene in the movie *The Day After Tomorrow* where floodwaters engulf New York—an irresistible force steadily closing in, the familiar world suddenly thrown into chaos, and the audience left to witness the unparalleled power of nature.

Players also love this sense of tension. Many gamers with high-end PCs have recorded the entire sequence of the “Giant Wave” event at maximum 4K settings and shared the footage online. Especially after the Sky Harbor map was upgraded with UE5 technology, Unreal Engine 5 features like Nanite and Lumen have made the sight of the giant wave crashing into the city look incredibly realistic.“My graphics card is about to catch fire!” is the most common comment under these videos; others joke, “This is the wave Delta has been waiting for his whole life.”

Even in overseas comment sections, quite a few players have been comparing Delta’s gameplay footage to blockbusters like *Battlefield*, and their comments are full of love.

For a long time, we’ve taken for granted the dominance of overseas AAA titles in terms of physical destruction and lighting effects, praising *Call of Duty* for its lighting details and *Battlefield* for its environmental destruction—yet it remains rare for domestic FPS games to receive similar recognition.

This may mean that, at long last, a Chinese-developed FPS game has, through its top-notch performance, broken into the technical arena where overseas FPS games have long held a leading position.

So how did *Operation Delta*, which has been live for two years, pull this off?With this question in mind, I spoke with the lead designer of the “Operation Delta” Comprehensive Battlefield Skyport map, a technical artist, and the head of the engine team. Through their accounts, I saw three distinct aspects: a solid technical foundation, the tenacity to tackle seemingly impossible challenges, and a creator’s heart that remains steadfastly focused on the player experience.

01

Putting an Elephant in a Refrigerator

“The whole process is like putting an elephant in a refrigerator—it’s an epic challenge,” the lead designer at Skyport told me.

The essence of huge waves is water, and simulating water has always been difficult—this is a consensus within the game development industry. Mathematical modeling of waveforms, the sorting of reflections, refractions, and transparent objects; plus water bodies of different locations and types, each with its own color, turbidity, and flow state—each of these requires extremely complex algorithms to implement.Furthermore, according to technical artists, rendering realistic water in a film or TV scene can take dozens of hours to compute a single shot, whereas in a multiplayer FPS, there are only a few milliseconds available for rendering.

Not to mention, in Delta, characters can dive, swim, and operate boats—which requires consideration of the interactions between the water environment, vehicles, and operator skills, as well as ensuring server synchronization in multiplayer mode. Achieving this level of interactivity has already required a tremendous amount of R&D effort.Scale this aquatic environment up a thousand or even ten thousand times, and both the technical difficulty and performance demands skyrocket exponentially. Even when looking at the global multiplayer FPS landscape, they can find almost no direct precedents to draw upon.

“At the first meeting, everyone gasped—‘How could you design something this difficult?’” recalled the technical art specialist, but he quickly added, “Everyone said it was hard, but they were actually really looking forward to bringing it to life.”After all, the idea of “creating waves” at Skyport was so perfectly fitting—it would serve as the emotional catharsis for this epic battle between G.T.I. and Hafke Sky City.

After several rounds of internal discussions, the project team decided to adopt a phased delivery plan: first, they would build a minimum viable demo capable of showcasing the “giant wave” effect to confirm that it could run in its basic form on both PC and mobile platforms; then, they would break down the required artistic details and interactive effects into separate components, implementing them layer by layer and building upon each other.

Multiple teams—including Art, 3C, Technical Art, Design and Engine, Visual Effects, and Performance—were all mobilized.During this period, the technical artists were busy becoming “giant wave experts”—they extensively reviewed academic papers on tsunamis and mathematical modeling of ocean water, and also referenced the fluid dynamics depictions in films such as *2012* and *Haeyundae*, all in pursuit of a single answer:How can we use algorithms to model this ever-changing body of water created by the massive waves?

“Tsunamis in nature are completely different from still water: when they first form, they start as an extremely slow wave, then the wave continues to expand and energy builds up layer by layer until it crashes head-on into the shore, at which point it slows down in certain areas.” A technical art specialist gave an example. They recreated these morphological changes in the game, so players can see them more clearly when looking down from an airplane as the giant wave approaches.

There were also some water effects featuring massive waves that we had to abandon after testing because it was nearly impossible to avoid this long-standing optimization challenge—the massive waves themselves are rendered as full-screen water effects, and when combined with scene fragmentation, splashes, water mist, and skill effects, along with dozens of players and vehicles on the same screen, how could we possibly reduce the performance overhead?

A technical art specialist told me, “There’s no silver bullet for optimization”—every department has to fine-tune the details bit by bit.Specifically for water rendering, they developed a GPU-based software subdivision solution: increasing the mesh density of water in the foreground, reducing it in real time in the background, and precisely removing meshes that players cannot see—all to minimize the rendering overhead for every frame as much as possible.

The final result is that the overall shape of the giant wave is driven by specialized algorithms and curves, with Gerstner waves superimposed on the wave body to add detail to the undulations. As the giant wave advances, the overall color of the water deepens and its turbidity increases, causing this stretch of water to constantly change over time.

These details—which players might inadvertently overlook—combine with a smooth gaming environment to shape the ultimate experience——In real life, people rarely have the chance to face massive waves head-on, but in the game, they can take on the role of a G.T.I. agent and personally experience this overwhelming sense of pressure coming from all directions, allowing the tension that has built up throughout the entire battle to be released all at once in that moment.

02

Amid the Waves

At this point, the wave’s structure has taken shape. But the project is only halfway complete. The other half involves taking the concept a step further. “We don’t just want to create the water itself and make it look better; we also want to build a series of interactions around it to make the threat posed by the giant wave feel more believable to players.”

Fortunately, they’ve accumulated a wide range of visual techniques over the years. For example, from last year’s “Eye of the Storm” map to this year’s “Aftershock” map, Delta has developed a suite of techniques ranging from all-terrain tactical destruction to large-scale building destruction—techniques that are perfectly suited to showcasing the destructive power of giant waves.

One clever touch is that, just as the wave is about to reach the player’s location,the G.T.I. landing craft is swept up by the wave and crashes violently into a building where the player had just been engaged in fierce combat—instantly bringing the sheer power of the wave to life while also adding a sense of G.T.I.’s “do-or-die” situation.

The planners then broke down the scripted events into three acts—before, during, and after the giant wave strikes—and assigned them to various modules such as visuals, audio, and UI. Before the wave hits, the wind swirls violently, flocks of crows take flight in panic, and air-raid sirens blare from all directions.The dynamic weather changes accordingly, and the HUD inside the visor suffers from electromagnetic interference. In the distance, billboards and vegetation have been torn up; water sprays into the air, and a wall of mist sweeps toward the viewer, fully capturing the atmosphere of “a storm is brewing.”

At the same time, they must also consider another issue—continuity and synchronization. In other words, this major event must unfold continuously; players must experience a “what you see is what you get” experience—from where the main wave advances to when operators are hit, and when vehicles and the environment respond. Everyone should also be able to remain actively engaged in the major event at all times.

For example, quite a few players felt after trying it out that “G.T.I. Superman” was a bit over-the-top—when an operator is knocked down by a giant wave, they don’t leave the screen immediately but instead enter an 8-second hit animation, making it look as if they’re “taking the brunt of the wave with their own body.”However, a technical art specialist told me, “If we followed real-world logic—where a giant wave instantly eliminates a player, who is then redeployed—it would actually be a hundred times easier to implement.”

He gave a few examples: “Suppose the player’s screen shows that a massive wave is still far away, but the server determines that the player has already been swept up by it—the sense of immersion is instantly shattered. Or suppose the position of a player jet-skiing or driving a boat in the water isn’t detected correctly, causing the water to appear to pass through the model.”If players were forced to remain in a death animation or a pre-rendered cutscene, none of these issues would need to be addressed. After numerous discussions with the combat engineering team, they ultimately chose the more resource-intensive solution: allowing players to witness the entire event in real time.

The team chose the path with the steepest technical challenge and developed a solution called “Water Tsunami,” which separates the system into a logic layer and a rendering layer: a deterministic function driven by server time “t” ensures millisecond-level synchronization of the giant wave state across the server CPU, client CPU, and GPU, which is then used to render the main wave body and generate interactive feedback.At the same time, they used their in-house water simulation tool, Water ACT, to pre-compute data describing the water environment, enabling them to determine as accurately as possible when players were on the surface, when they were underwater, and when they should switch between different states such as swimming or diving.

Many of the game’s most breathtaking in-game highlights stem from this kind of “grind.” Real-time participation opens up even more possibilities for gameplay—some players use the Silverwing Agent to release a falcon from the top of a skyscraper and watch it soar over the towering waves; others hop into an amphibious vehicle to enjoy the sensation of sinking to the bottom and then resurfacing;some do absolutely nothing, simply savoring the sensation of being knocked over by the waves; and we’ve even seen players posting videos specifically to promote this “must-try activity” at Skyport: hopping on a jet ski and riding the crest of the waves at their peak.

Especially when you enable the “Realistic Mode” graphics option—which utilizes UE5 features—the details of the wave, the city’s lighting and shadows, and the interactions unfolding before your eyes all blend together, allowing everyone to experience a unique “giant wave crashing” sequence from their own perspective.

After listening to the R&D team describe these efforts, I realized that no matter how deeply the discussion delved into technical details, it always came back to the same thing: the player experience.

As the massive wave sweeps through, players find themselves on what feels like a brand-new battlefield, surrounded by rubble and ruins.The two outposts where fierce battles had raged earlier were closed off after being struck by the massive wave, and the new outpost was relocated to the rooftop of a skyscraper. Both sides entered a confrontation with unlimited troops, and the attacking side could even deploy forces from the air. The entire battle shifted from a ground-based advance to vertical attacks and defenses between skyscrapers, completely rewriting the dynamics of the battlefield.

So, what exactly did this massive wave bring to the Delta? It not only allowed players to experience a visual spectacle firsthand, but also transformed that sensory impact into a new combat experience.After the game ends, the slogan “Capture the South Bank” displayed on the screen hints at entirely new possibilities for future battles in Skyport. The giant wave has thus become a tangible, massive variable within the tactical landscape.

03

The more difficult the journey, the more wondrous the sights.

Looking back on the entire R&D process, it’s quite moving.Behind a map event lasting just a few minutes lies the close collaboration and repeated iterations of multiple departments within the Delta team, who overcame a series of technical challenges. As the game enters its long-term operation phase, many teams opt for a “play it safe” approach—doing less to minimize mistakes. So why did TiMi J3 choose to take on such a difficult task?

“Looking back, it seems as though the team has been constantly reaching new heights in user experience, but in reality, the groundwork for many of these seemingly unattainable goals was laid long ago during previous R&D efforts,” the head of the engine team told me.

This statement also reveals a core strategic barrier for the team: technological compounding. Juwang is a prime example: as longtime Delta players know, there is actually a subtle, underlying thread of aquatic research and development running through it.

For example, over the first four seasons, the team studied aquatic ecology during the early stages of development. These deep, low-level “modifications” underpin the implementation of Delta’s various features.

title: 영화 《델타 작전》 제작진과의 대담: 거친 파도 속의 산업적 야망과 해답
text:
재난 영화를 본 적이 있나요? 《델타 작전》의 UE5 업그레이드 후 새로운 시즌에서, 스카이포트 위로 수십 미터 높이의 거대한 파도가 밀려오는 모습을 올려다보며, 저는 왜 이런 장르의 영화가 영화사에서 오랫동안 사랑받아 왔는지 이해하게 되었습니다.
승리를 확정지을 유도 미사일이 떨어지자, 먼저 항구 전체를 뒤흔드는 거대한 폭발음이 울려 퍼졌고, 곧이어 거대한 파도가 밀려와 도로와 교량, 건물들을 강타하며 하얀 물보라를 일으켰다.파도가 가까워질수록 그 파괴력은 더욱 생생하게 드러났다. 파도는 지나가는 길의 건물들을 산산조각 내고, 차량과 나무, 가로등, 거대한 철근 콘크리트 파편들을 휩쓸어 갔으며, 안전 지대로 피신할 틈도 없었던 G.T.I. 요원들마저 함께 휩쓸려 갔다.
망비
이 장면은 영화 《투모로우》에서 홍수가 뉴욕을 덮치는 장면을 떠올리지 않을 수 없게 만든다. 저항할 수 없는 힘이 끊임없이 다가오고, 익숙한 세상이 순식간에 혼란에 빠지면서, 관객들은 이를 통해 대자연의 비할 데 없는 위력을 실감하게 된다.
플레이어들도 이러한 긴장감을 매우 좋아합니다. 고사양 PC를 보유한 많은 플레이어들이 ‘거대한 파도’ 이벤트의 4K 최고 화질 전체 과정을 녹화해 온라인에 공유하고 있습니다. 특히 ‘스카이포트’ 맵이 UE5 기술로 업그레이드된 후, Nanite, Lumen 등 언리얼 5의 특징 덕분에 거대한 파도가 도시를 강타하는 장면이 더욱 실감 나게 표현되었습니다.“그래픽 카드가 타버릴 것 같아!”는 이런 영상 아래에서 가장 흔히 볼 수 있는 댓글이며, “이것이 바로 델타가 평생 기다려온 거대한 파도다”라고 농담을 하는 사람도 있습니다.
심지어 해외 댓글란에서도 상당수의 플레이어들이 델타의 실제 플레이 영상을 《배틀필드》 같은 대작들과 비교하며, 글 곳곳에서 애정이 묻어나고 있다.
오랜 기간 동안 우리는 해외 3A 게임들이 물리적 파괴와 조명 렌더링 분야에서 보여주는 압도적인 우위를 당연시해 왔으며, 《콜 오브 듀티》의 세밀한 조명 표현과 《배틀필드》의 장면 파괴 효과를 칭찬해 왔지만, 중국산 FPS 게임이 이와 유사한 인정을 받는 경우는 여전히 드물다.
이는 아마도 드디어 한 중국산 FPS 게임이 뛰어난 성능을 바탕으로, 해외 FPS가 오랫동안 주도해 온 기술 우위 영역에 진입했음을 의미할지도 모른다.
그렇다면 출시된 지 2년이 된 ‘델타’는 어떻게 이를 해낸 것일까?이 질문을 안고, 『델타 작전』의 ‘전면 전장: 스카이포트’ 맵 기획 책임자, 기술 아트 전문가, 엔진 팀 책임자를 찾아갔다. 그들의 이야기를 통해 나는 세 가지 뚜렷한 측면을 확인할 수 있었다. 바로 탄탄한 기술적 기반, 불가능함을 알면서도 도전하는 투지, 그리고 언제나 플레이어 경험을 최우선으로 여기는 창작자의 마음이었다.
01
코끼리를 냉장고에 넣기
“전체 과정은 마치 코끼리를 냉장고에 넣는 것과 같아서, 그 난이도는 정말 어마어마합니다.” 스카이포트 기획 책임자가 내게 말했다.
거대한 파도의 본질은 물이며, 물의 구현은 항상 어려웠다는 점은 게임 개발계의 공통된 인식입니다. 파형의 수학적 모델링, 반사, 굴절, 투명한 물체의 순서 지정; 또한 위치와 유형이 다른 수역마다 각기 다른 색상, 탁도, 흐름 상태를 구현하기 위해서는 모든 항목마다 매우 복잡한 알고리즘이 필요합니다.게다가 기술 아트 담당자들의 말에 따르면, 사실적인 물체를 영화나 TV 장면 속에 배치할 경우, 한 샷을 렌더링하는 데 수십 시간이 소요될 수 있지만, 멀티플레이어 FPS 게임에서는 렌더링에 할당된 시간이 고작 몇 밀리초에 불과하다.
더욱이 델타는 물속에서 잠수하고, 헤엄치고, 배를 운전할 수 있기 때문에, 수역과 탈것, 요원의 스킬 간의 상호작용을 고려해야 할 뿐만 아니라, 멀티플레이어 모드에서 서버 동기화를 보장해야 하므로, 이러한 상호작용을 구현하는 데만도 막대한 연구 개발 노력이 투입되었습니다.이러한 수중 환경을 수천, 수만 배로 확대하면 기술적 난이도와 성능 부담은 기하급수적으로 급증합니다. 심지어 전 세계 멀티플레이어 FPS 분야를 통틀어 봐도 직접 참고할 만한 사례를 거의 찾아볼 수 없습니다.
“첫 회의에서 다들 ‘어떻게 이렇게 어려운 걸 디자인했냐’며 깜짝 놀랐죠.” 기술 미술 전문가가 회상했지만, 곧 말을 이어갔다. “다들 입으로는 어렵다고 했지만, 사실은 이걸 실제로 만들어내는 걸 무척 기대하고 있었어요.” 어쨌든 스카이포트에서 ‘파도 만들기’라는 아이디어는 너무나도 자연스러웠고, 이는 G.T.I.와 하프크 스카이시티 간의 대결에서 감정이 폭발하는 지점이 될 것이기 때문이다.
이에 내부에서 몇 차례 논의를 거친 끝에, 프로젝트 팀은 단계별delivery 계획을 채택하기로 결정했다. 먼저 거대한 파도 효과를 구현할 수 있는 최소 실행 가능 데모(MVP)를 제작하여, PC와 모바일 양 플랫폼에서 파도 효과가 기본적으로 정상 작동하는지 확인한 뒤, 구현해야 할 그래픽 디테일과 인터랙션 효과를 분리하여 단계별로 구현하고 차근차근 쌓아가는 방식이다.
미술, 3C, 기술 미술, 기획 및 엔진, 특수 효과 및 시뮬레이션 등 여러 팀이 총동원되었다.이 기간 동안 기술 아트 팀원들은 ‘거대한 파도 전문가’가 되기 위해 분주히 움직였습니다. 그들은 쓰나미와 해양 수체의 수학적 모델링에 관한 학술 논문을 광범위하게 조사했고, 《2012》, 《해운대》 등의 영화 및 드라마 작품에서 표현된 유체 역학 장면도 참고하며, 오직 하나의 해답을 찾기 위해 노력했습니다.알고리즘을 통해 끊임없이 변화하는 이 거대한 파도의 물체를 어떻게 묘사할 수 있을까?
“자연계의 쓰나미는 고요한 수역과는 특징이 완전히 다릅니다. 처음 생성될 때는 매우 완만한 파도이지만, 파도가 계속 확대되면서 에너지가 층층이 축적되다가 해안과 정면으로 부딪히면 일부 구역에서는 다시 속도가 느려집니다.” 기술 미술 전문가가 예를 들었다. 그들은 이러한 형태 변화를 게임에 재현했으며, 플레이어는 거대한 파도가 밀려올 때 비행기에서 내려다보면 이를 더 선명하게 볼 수 있다.
테스트 결과, 일부 거대한 파도의 물 효과는 포기할 수밖에 없었습니다. 이 오랜 난제를 해결하는 데 있어서는 피할 수 없는 문제였기 때문입니다. 거대한 파도 자체는 화면 전체를 덮는 물 렌더링이며, 여기에 장면 파편, 물보라, 물안개, 스킬 효과까지 더해지고, 화면에는 수십 명의 플레이어와 탈것이 함께 등장하는데, 어떻게 하면 성능 부담을 줄일 수 있을까요?
기술 아트 전문가는 “최적화에 만능 해결책은 없다”며, 각 부서마다 세부 사항을 하나하나 꼼꼼히 다듬어야 한다고 말했습니다.특히 물 렌더링의 경우, 그들은 GPU 기반의 소프트웨어 서브디비전 솔루션을 개발했습니다. 가까운 곳에서는 물의 메쉬 밀도를 높이고, 먼 곳에서는 실시간으로 밀도를 낮추며, 플레이어가 볼 수 없는 메쉬는 정밀하게 제거함으로써 프레임당 렌더링 부하를 최대한 줄였습니다.
최종 결과물에서는 거대한 파도의 전체적인 형태가 전용 알고리즘과 곡선에 의해 제어되며, 파도 표면에는 게르스트너 파동이 중첩되어 파도의 기복에 디테일을 더합니다. 거대한 파도가 밀려오면서 물의 전체적인 색이 짙어지고 탁도도 높아져, 이 수역이 시간이 지남에 따라 끊임없이 변화하는 모습을 보여줍니다.
이 플레이어들이 무심코 지나칠 수도 있는 세부 요소들이 쌓이고, 여기에 원활한 실행 환경이 더해져 최종적인 경험을 결정짓습니다——현실에서는 거대한 파도를 직접 마주할 기회가 거의 없지만, 게임 속에서는 G.T.I. 요원이 되어 사방에서 밀려오는 압박감을 몸소 체험할 수 있으며, 전투 내내 쌓여온 긴장감이 바로 이 순간에 한꺼번에 터져 나옵니다.
02
파도 속에서
이 단계에서 거대한 파도의 형태는 이미 완성되었습니다. 하지만 이 거대한 프로젝트는 아직 절반밖에 끝나지 않았습니다. 나머지 절반은 기획 단계에서 한 걸음 더 나아간 고민에서 비롯됩니다. “우리는 단순히 물 자체를 만들고 더 멋지게 보이게 하는 데 그치지 않고, 이를 중심으로 일련의 상호작용을 전개하여 거대한 파도가 주는 위협이 플레이어에게 더욱 실감 나게 느껴지도록 해야 합니다.”
다행히도, 그들은 지금까지 다양한 표현 수단을 축적해 왔습니다. 예를 들어, 작년의 ‘폭풍의 눈’ 맵부터 올해 초의 ‘여진’ 맵에 이르기까지, 델타는 전 지형에 걸친 전술적 파괴부터 대규모 건물 파괴에 이르기까지 일련의 기술을 축적해 왔습니다. 이는 거대한 파도의 파괴력을 보여주기에 안성맞춤입니다.
여기에는 한 가지 기발한 아이디어가 있는데, 파도가 플레이어가 있는 위치에 거의 도달할 무렵,G.T.I. 측의 상륙정이 파도에 휩쓸려, 플레이어가 방금 전까지 치열한 전투를 벌이던 건물에 굉음을 내며 충돌하는 장면입니다. 이를 통해 거대한 파도의 위력이 한눈에 생생하게 드러날 뿐만 아니라, G.T.I. 측의 ‘등에 물을 등지고 싸우는’ 절박한 분위기도 한층 더해집니다.
기획자는 거대한 파도가 닥치기 전, 도중, 후의 3막 구조에 따라 시나리오 이벤트를 분할하여 영상, 오디오, UI 등 각 모듈에 배분한다. 거대한 파도가 닥치기 전, 바람이 거세게 휘몰아치고 까마귀 떼가 흩어지며 사방에서 공습 경보가 울려 퍼진다.이에 따라 날씨도 변화하며, 헬멧 안의 HUD는 전자기 간섭을 받는다. 멀리서 몇몇 광고판과 초목이 이미 휩쓸려 나가고, 물보라가 치솟으며, 수증기가 하늘을 뒤덮고 눈앞으로 밀려와 “폭풍우가 몰려오기 전의 긴장감”을 극도로 고조시킨다.
동시에 그들은 또 다른 문제, 즉 지속성과 동기화 문제도 고려해야 합니다. 다시 말해, 이 대규모 이벤트는 지속적으로 진행되어야 하며, 메인 웨이브가 어디까지 진행되는지, 요원이 언제 공격을 받는지, 차량과 배경이 언제 반응하는지 등 모든 것이 플레이어가 보는 그대로 반영되어야 합니다. 또한 모든 플레이어가 이 대규모 이벤트에 지속적으로 참여할 수 있어야 합니다.
예를 들어, 꽤 많은 플레이어들이 체험 후 “G.T.I. 슈퍼맨”의 표현이 다소 과장되었다고 느꼈습니다. 요원이 거대한 파도에 휩쓸려 넘어져도 바로 퇴장하지 않고, 8초 동안 지속되는 피격 애니메이션이 재생되는데, 마치 “육체로 거대한 파도를 버티는” 듯한 느낌입니다.하지만 기술 미술 전문가는 저에게 “현실적인 논리에 따라 파도에 한 번 맞으면 플레이어가 즉시 제거되고 재배치되는 방식을 적용한다면, 오히려 구현하기가 백 배는 더 쉬울 것”이라고 말했습니다.
그는 몇 가지 예를 들었다. “만약 플레이어의 화면상으로는 거대한 파도가 아직 멀리 있는데, 서버가 플레이어가 이미 파도에 휩쓸렸다고 판정한다면 몰입감이 순식간에 깨져버린다. 또 플레이어가 물속에서 제트 추진을 하거나 배를 조종할 때 위치 감지가 정확하지 않으면, 물의 렌더링에 모델링 오류가 발생한다.”플레이어를 강제로 사망 애니메이션이나 미리 제작된 컷신 속에 가둬버린다면, 앞서 언급한 문제들은 모두 고려할 필요가 없다. 그들은 전투 기술 팀과 여러 차례 논의한 끝에, 비용이 더 많이 드는 방안을 선택했다. 바로 플레이어가 사건의 전 과정을 실시간으로 지켜볼 수 있도록 하는 것이다.
팀은 기술적 난이도가 가장 높은 길을 선택하고, ‘Water Tsunami’라는 솔루션을 제시하여 이벤트를 논리 계층과 렌더링 계층으로 분리했습니다. 서버 시간 t를 기반으로 결정론적 함수를 구동하여 서버 CPU, 클라이언트 CPU 및 GPU 내의 거대한 파도 상태를 밀리초 단위로 동기화한 뒤, 이를 바탕으로 주 파도 체의 렌더링과 상호작용 피드백을 완성했습니다.이와 동시에, 자체 개발한 수체 툴인 ‘Water ACT’를 통해 데이터를 사전 계산하여 수체 데이터를 표현함으로써, 플레이어가 언제 수면 위에 있고 언제 수면 아래에 있는지, 언제 수영이나 잠수 등 다른 상태로 전환해야 하는지를 최대한 정확하게 판단했습니다.
게임 내에서 볼 수 있는 수많은 놀라운 하이라이트 장면들도 모두 이런 ‘꾸준한 노력’에서 비롯된 것입니다. 실시간 참여는 게임 플레이에 더 많은 가능성을 부여합니다. 어떤 이는 ‘실버윙’ 요원을 이용해 고층 빌딩 옥상에서 매를 날려 거대한 파도를 내려다보기도 하고, 어떤 이는 수륙양용 차량에 올라타 바닥으로 가라앉았다가 다시 떠오르는 과정을 즐기기도 하며;어떤 이는 아예 아무것도 하지 않고 파도에 휩쓸려 넘어지는 느낌만 즐기기도 했고; 심지어 이번 ‘스카이포트’의 ‘꼭 해봐야 할 체험’을 소개하는 영상을 올리는 플레이어도 있었는데, 바로 제트스키를 타고 파도가 가장 거세질 때 파도 정점을 타고 서핑을 즐기는 것이었습니다.
특히 UE5의 기능을 활용한 ‘다큐멘터리 모드’ 화질 옵션을 활성화하면, 파도의 디테일과 도시의 빛과 그림자, 그리고 눈앞에서 끊임없이 펼쳐지는 상호작용이 어우러져, 누구나 자신만의 시점에서 각기 다른 ‘거대한 파도가 밀려오는’ 장면을 경험할 수 있습니다.
연구개발 팀이 이러한 노력에 대해 설명하는 것을 듣고 나니, 대화가 아무리 깊은 기술적 세부 사항으로 빠져들더라도 결국에는 항상 같은 점, 즉 플레이어의 경험으로 돌아온다는 것을 깨달았습니다.
이 거대한 파도가 휩쓸고 지나간 후, 주변의 폐허를 바라보며 플레이어는 마치 새로운 전장에 서 있는 듯한 느낌을 받는다.앞서 치열한 전투가 벌어졌던 두 거점은 거대한 파도의 충격을 받고 폐쇄되었고, 새로운 거점은 고층 빌딩 옥상으로 옮겨졌다. 양측은 무한한 병력을 동원해 대치하게 되었으며, 공격 측은 공중에서도 병력을 투입할 수 있게 되었다. 전투는 지상에서 시작되어 고층 빌딩 사이의 수직 공방전으로 전환되며, 전장의 공방 구도가 다시 한번 재편되었다.
그렇다면, 이 거대한 파도는 델타에 도대체 무엇을 가져다주었을까? 이는 플레이어에게 단순히 시각적 경이로움을 직접 체험하게 해준 것뿐만 아니라, 이러한 감각적 충격을 새로운 전투 경험으로 이어지게 했다.게임이 끝난 후, 화면에 나타난 “남쪽 강변 점령”이라는 문구는 스카이포트에서 펼쳐질 향후 전장의 새로운 가능성을 암시하고 있습니다. 거대한 파도는 이로써 전술적 공간에서 실질적으로 존재하는 거대한 변수로 자리 잡게 되었습니다.
03
그 과정은 더욱 어려워질수록, 그 결과는 더욱 놀랍다
이제 와서 전체 연구 개발 과정을 되돌아보니 꽤 감회가 깊습니다.단 몇 분짜리 맵 대형 이벤트 뒤에는 델타 팀의 여러 부서가 긴밀히 협력하고 반복적인 개선을 거쳐 일련의 기술적 난관을 극복한 과정이 숨어 있습니다. 장기 운영 단계에 접어들면 많은 팀이 ‘안정성을 최우선으로 삼아, 적게 할수록 실수도 적다’는 방식을 택하는데, 티미 J3는 왜 굳이 이렇게 어려운 일을 자처했을까요?
“돌이켜보면, 팀은 줄곧 사용자 경험의 새로운 차원을 개척해 온 것처럼 보이지만, 사실 겉보기에는 도저히 달성할 수 없을 것 같던 많은 목표들은 이미 과거의 연구 개발 과정에서 그 기반이 마련되어 있었습니다.” 엔진 팀 책임자가 내게 말했다.
이 말은 또한 팀의 핵심적인 전략적 장벽인 ‘기술의 복리 효과’를 드러내고 있습니다. ‘거랑’이 바로 그 전형적인 사례입니다. 오래된 ‘델타’ 유저라면 누구나 알다시피, 그 이면에는 마치 얇은 실처럼 은은하게 이어지는 수역 연구 개발의 흐름이 숨어 있습니다.
예를 들어 지난 네 시즌 동안, 팀은 초기 연구 개발 단계에서 수생태학을 연구했으며, ‘아름다운 물’을 만드는 방법을 점차 파악해 나갔고, 기술을 통해 물의 색상, 탁도, 굴절률 등의 물리적 특성을 어떻게 표현할지 탐구했습니다. 창궁 계곡과 제0호 댐의 광활한 수역에서, 지역별로 서로 다른 시각적 효과를 연출해 냈습니다.
S5부터 델타는 공식적으로 다이빙과 수영 플레이를 도입하며, ‘보기 좋은 물’에서 ‘놀 수 있는 물’로 한 단계 도약했습니다 . 개발팀은 이 시점부터 자체 개발한 물 체인 도구 체인인 ‘Water ACT’를 유지 관리하기 시작했으며, 수역 생성, 데이터 생성, 구성 및 점검 등의 프로세스를 통합하여 기획자와 아티스트가 아이디어를 더 빠르게 검증할 수 있도록 했습니다.그 후 팀은 매 시즌 업데이트 요구 사항에 따라 툴체인에 지속적으로 새로운 기능을 추가해 왔습니다. 예를 들어, 이번 ‘거대한 파도’에서 렌더링과 게임플레이 판정을 연결하는 데 사용된 사전 계산된 물 데이터 역시 이 툴체인을 통해 생성되었습니다.
이미 2024년에 델타 팀은 GDC 무대에 올라 전 세계 개발자들에게 프로덕션 파이프라인을 소개했습니다.
이 뒤에는 전담 엔진 팀이 조용히 전체 연구개발 체계를 뒷받침하고 있습니다.엔진 팀 책임자는 물 효과 솔루션 외에도 지형, 조명, 오픈 월드, PCG, 텍스처, 식생, 렌더링 파이프라인, 그리고 다양한 호환성 조정 등을 중심으로 맞춤형 작업을 진행했으며, 심지어 스트리밍 로딩과 직렬화까지 개조했다고 말했습니다. 이러한 저수준에 이르는 ‘대대적인 개조’가 델타의 각종 기능 구현을 뒷받침하고 있습니다.
이제 그들은 Nanite, Lumen, VSM 등 UE5 기능을 델타(Delta)라는 심도 있게 맞춤화된 자체 개발 제작 파이프라인에 정식으로 통합했습니다 . 버전 출시를 유지하면서 동시에 기반 기술 수준을 한 단계 끌어올리고 있습니다. 성능 최적화 측면에서도, 그들은 한 달 동안 상위 계층의 기능부터 하위 계층의 멀티스레드 스케줄링에 이르기까지 대대적인 개조를 단행하여 수만 줄의 코드를 추가함으로써, 동일한 그래픽 카드에서 게임의 기본 프레임률을 70~80프레임에서 120프레임 이상으로 끌어올렸습니다(UE5의 공식 목표는 60프레임이다)——이는 프로듀서 Shadow가 그들에게 제시한 ‘필수 요구사항’이었다.
델타 팀이 올해 언리얼 페스트(Unreal Fest)에서 일부 성과를 발표했을 때, 한 업계 관계자가 ‘차관군’에게 그들이 한 일이 “상상조차 할 수 없을 정도”라고 속삭였다고 한다.
둘째, 플레이어에게 지속적으로 훌륭한 게임 경험을 선사하는 것이 우리 팀이 끊임없이 어려운 과제를 해결해 나가는 원동력입니다. 기술이 한 걸음 나아갈 때마다 우리는 항상 같은 질문을 던집니다. ‘이 기술이 플레이어에게 어떤 새로운 경험을 선사할 수 있을까?’
역시 ‘물’이라는 요소를 예로 들어보겠습니다. 델타의 ‘물’에 대한 탐구는 그 흔적을 찾을 수 있을 뿐만 아니라, 매 시즌마다 플레이어의 전술적 결정과 게임 경험을 변화시키곤 합니다. 이는 꽤 이례적인 일입니다.
