编者按

本文来自 GDC 官方 Youtube 频道的《GDC 2023》合集，原内容形式为视频演讲。目前，indienova 已取得 GDC Youtube 频道的视频转文稿译制授权，未来将持续进行 GDC 历年精华演讲的编译整理工作，以图文形式分享。

应版权方要求，我们将在每篇文章的文首嵌入原 Youtube 视频。考虑到可能存在的播放问题，我们将继续与 GDC 官方沟通，力图为国内读者带来更便利的呈现形式和更舒适的阅读/观看体验。

  • 演讲人：Yngvill Hopen
  • 译者：1145

视频：《Flopping Successfully: Running a Studio Without a Huge Hit》

前言

我是 Yngvill Hopen，一名视觉艺术家。我的艺术生涯始于传统艺术领域，但游戏的魅力让我最终转向了游戏行业。目前，我在挪威西部常年潮湿的城市卑尔根经营着一家名为 Henchman & Goon 的小型工作室。尽管我的身份依然是艺术家——就在几年前，我还获得了概念艺术的学位，但经营工作室让我体验到了不同的工作方式，我需要在团队中协作，这正是我非常享受的部分。

《Flem》《Pode》以及《Pode Kids》

大约 11 年前，我和一群刚从大学毕业的朋友共同创办了 Henchman & Goon。截至目前，我们一共发布了三款游戏：第一款是《Flem》，一款 PC 端的小型 2D 平台游戏；第二款是《Pode》，这是我们迄今为止发布的规模最大、最具野心的作品，支持 PC 和主机平台；第三款是《Pode Kids》，这是我们去年夏天在 Google Play 上推出的儿童活动应用。我们还有三款游戏正处于不同的开发阶段，不过本次演讲中，我想着重聊一聊《Pode》。

我们从 2015 年开始开发《Pode》，那时距离创立 Henchman & Goon 过去了大约三年。整个开发过程持续了三年，期间大部分时间由四人核心团队负责，时不时会短期增加一两名成员。直到开发最后六个月，开发团队幸运地扩大到了七人，并有音效和音乐制作人员加入。2018 年 6 月，《Pode》在 Switch 平台正式发布，但市场表现却不尽如人意。坦白说，那个夏天对我们所有人来说都并不愉快。然而，事情最终迎来了转机，关于这一点，我稍后会详细展开。

艺术家也要吃饭

我想先简单介绍一下我的成长背景。我成长于一个艺术氛围浓厚的家庭，家人多为艺术家、音乐家、演员和创意工作者。从记事起，我就一直在进行艺术创作，在艺术领域取得成功的观念也深深扎根于我的生活。我很早就下定决心要以艺术为生。而一旦确立了这个目标，你就会开始思考，成为一名成功或失败的艺术家究竟意味着什么。同时，你也会在作品和艺术风格上产生好胜心，甚至对成功艺术家的形象变得有些执着。

艺术家的形象

我自然也不例外，也曾经历过那种年轻气盛、自命不凡的艺术家阶段。那时，我将自己的身份认同与我心中艺术家的形象紧密联系在一起。老实说，年轻时我们常常被一些陈词滥调影响，从而形成这些观念。其中一个典型观念是：你必须为艺术受苦，将全部自我投入到艺术中，绝不能让平庸的生活妨碍艺术的伟大。因此，当有人建议我除了艺术创作外，或许还需要考虑一些其他事情，比如找一份有薪水的工作时，我有时会有些抵触。难道除了从灵魂深处创作艺术，我还需要做其他事情吗？

我妈妈对我的自负从来没什么耐心，她只是告诉我：“艺术家也要吃饭。”从字面上看，这句话很简单——每个人都需要吃饭。但在当时的语境下，它还意味着我和其他人并没有什么不同，我们都需要为了生活而做一些必要的事情。这既是生理需求，也是作为社会成员的责任。我们不能简单决定成为某类人，并宣称自己拥有特权，从而免于承担其他所有责任。妈妈的这句话在我需要时让我清醒过来，我带着这句话去面对之后的每一件事，包括创办 Henchman & Goon，这在后来的故事中变得尤为重要。

创业初期

让我们回到创办 Henchman & Goon 的故事。正如我之前提到的，工作室成立时，我们大多数人刚从大学毕业。虽然其中一些人已经做了一段时间自由职业，对小企业的经营略知一二，但大多数时候，我们对这段冒险真正意味着什么几乎一无所知。我们之所以想要创办自己的工作室，有很充分的理由：我们渴望创作自由，每个人都有自己想实现的创意；我们希望继续和朋友们一起工作，并为自己建立一番事业；然而最重要的是，我们想做游戏，而当时本地没有这样的工作机会，甚至几乎没有游戏工作室。因此，如果我们想留在家乡，同时又不放弃梦想，创办自己的工作室基本上是唯一选择。

作为一群经验尚浅的游戏开发者，我们该如何迈出第一步？制定计划似乎是个不错的开始，而这个计划的首要任务就是存活。无论是艺术创作还是游戏开发，都需要时间，因此，为了实现目标，我们必须确保在游戏开发过程中能够维持生计。在工作室成立后的三年里，我们主要依靠合同项目和兼职来维持运作。所谓合同项目，指的是为本地餐厅设计菜单、制作书籍封面等工作。同时，我们也在空闲时间开发小型游戏。我们并不介意这样的状态，因为我们清楚自己的计划。我们正一步步向目标迈进——最终摆脱合同项目，全身心投入到工作室的游戏开发中。

大约在工作室成立三年后，我们终于发布了《Flem》。原本，我们预期这款游戏能带来一定收益。考虑到有限的预算，我们认为只要达到很少的销量，就能收回成本并赚取一些额外收入。当然，事情并没有按预期发展，但也不至于让我们大失所望。我们完成了游戏并将其推向市场，过程本身让我们感到欣慰。这个过程更像是一次实验——我们尝试打造属于自己的游戏，并从过程中学习。带着积累的经验，我们继续向前。

然而，创业的蜜月期已结束，我们不得不开始认真思考工作室的未来方向。大家逐渐有些厌倦必须依靠兼职来维持生计的生活。虽然我们尝试了其他项目，但都未能成功。项目资金难以筹得，团队在工作重心上的分歧也日益加剧。通过合同项目，我们已经积累了一批稳定的客户，同时一些合伙人发现，相较于游戏开发，他们对软件开发更感兴趣。这些年来，我们还吸引了更大、更具影响力的客户，他们为离岸业务提供了一些有趣的解决方案，这对我们来说利润可观。因此，在这个节点上，我们意识到，与其将团队朝着不同方向拉扯，不如将工作室拆分成两个独立团队。我们顺利地将工作室分为两个团队，过程中没有出现戏剧性冲突，团队关系仍旧和睦。我们依然共用同一间办公室，甚至在需要时共享人员和项目。留下来的团队专注于开发《Pode》，同时继续承接合同项目和兼职，朝着最终目标前行。

自从创办 Henchman & Goon 以来，我们一直在为各个项目寻求外部资金。尽管公司已成立四年，但我们仍在做那些本以为不会再涉足的事情——合同项目、兼职，以及各种与真正做游戏无关的工作。我们依然艰难求生，尚未实现盈利，但这并不意味着一无所获。我们积累了宝贵的财富：我们建立了一支彼此关心、合作愉快的团队，证明了自己有能力完成并成功发布项目。此外，我们投入大量时间，建立了一个庞大的社区，他们支持并相信着我们。正是这些努力，最终为我们赢得了项目资金，使我们得以完成《Pode》。尽管我们仍然需要承担一些外部工作，偶尔为资金奔波，但至少有三年时间，可以将主要精力投入到自己的项目中。这是充满了喜悦、泪水、压力和兴奋的三年。而最终将花费多年心血的作品发布出去时，那种感觉是无法用语言表达的。

因此，当结果不尽如人意时，那种打击绝对是令人心碎的。作为开发者，我们经常被告知，一款游戏必须卖出超过一万、两万份，甚至更多，才能被视为成功。而所谓的成功，当然是指收回成本并实现盈利。与其他项目相比，我们在这个项目上投入了更多的时间、资源和热爱，因此，失败带来的冲击也远非其他项目可比。我们曾告诉自己，这个项目将是推动我们迈向成功的关键一步，只要坚持到发布的那一天，一切都会变得容易。并且，这个项目还牵涉到员工、投资者，以及那些与我们签订了版税协议的合作伙伴，他们都依赖于我们，因此失败也会让这些人失望。那种感觉很像是经历了一场失去，你倾尽所有的热爱与能量打造美丽的事物，却在来到世界的瞬间就夭折了。

于是，你开始怀疑自己，思考是否还有坚持下去的意义。我们真的应该为了我们的艺术承受如此多的痛苦吗？然而，我们已经坚持了六年，尽管我们在思考未来是否还有希望，但最终还是回到了熟悉的事情上。我们重新接下合同项目，启动了一个新项目，同时也接了一些兼职，继续艰难求生。

转换视角

就在我们艰难求生的时候，奇怪的事情发生了。一款游戏发布后，其销量通常会在最初几周或几个月内达到高峰，随后便会大幅下降。因此，当游戏在发行初期销量不佳时，你会预期后续销量也会急转直下，回本更是成了遥不可及的梦想。然而，《Pode》的销量几乎没有出现任何下降。随着时间的推移，我们意识到，如果这种趋势能够持续下去，我们或许有机会实现回本的目标。

现在，我们必须重新振作，寻找前进方向。不过，我们的视角也稍微发生了转变，不再仅从计划维度出发，而是开始从优先级角度权衡选择。多年来，我们一直在用同样的方式运作，却收效甚微——尽管这让我们坚持到了现在。但问题是，我们是否愿意花费全部时间去追逐某种理想中的成功，却一次次经历失望的打击？于是，我们开始反思，重新审视自己拥有的一切：团队中彼此关心的伙伴，相信并支持我们的社区，我们的公司，我们在乎的项目，以及那份共同做游戏的热情。

我们制定了一份全新的优先级清单，虽然听起来清晰直接，但实际上，这一转变并非一蹴而就，而是经过循序渐进的视角调整才逐渐明确。首先，我们必须确保生存，如果连基本需求都得不到满足，那么创造更是无从谈起。同样重要的是，我们希望在创作美丽艺术和有趣游戏的同时，享受工作和生活的每一天。此外，我们不想再追逐某种虚无缥缈的未来目标。接下来，让我详细解释这份清单对我们的意义。

存活

存活意味着彼此关爱、相互扶持。这意味着团队中的每个人都在努力创造让大家都能感到安全和幸福的环境。要感到安全和幸福，人们需要体面的薪资、充足的食物和安稳的住所等基本条件；需要与家人和朋友共度时光，也需要属于自己的独处时光；需要被倾听，感受到自己的价值。这意味着，当开发工作过于紧张时，我们需要放慢节奏；我们需要允许人们有不那么高效的时候，因为每个人都会经历低谷或缺乏灵感的时刻，我们需要空间去过渡与重新振作，而不是因过度工作而走向崩溃；这同样意味着我们要打造能够激发灵感的环境，让每个人都能全情投入、发挥所长。换句话说，这意味着我们优先考虑人的需求，而项目则排在其次。

创作艺术并享受生活

你们可能都听过这样一句话：生活是在你忙于制定计划时悄然发生的。这句话很好地诠释了清单中的这一点。我们最初踏入游戏开发领域，是因为我们都是充满创意的人，喜欢创造新事物。在游戏开发变成工作之前，这也是我们闲暇时的乐趣。然而，如果工作变成了仅是按部就班地完成任务、制作产品，而职业生涯中唯一的高光时刻只是完成项目的那一天，那么这一切又有什么意义呢？但如果你热爱自己的作品，并享受创作的过程，那么回顾过去时，收获的将是快乐与成就感。另一方面，如果你能与自己的作品建立起深厚的联结，那么游戏发布后的所有工作也会变得更加轻松，无论是移植到新平台、运营社群，还是市场营销和公关，你能在做这些事情的过程中获得乐趣。

拥抱未知

最后，失望往往源于现实未能达到预期。如果你能调整好预期，就不会那么容易感到失望。这并不是说你不该全力以赴推出作品，也不是要你对一切持悲观态度，而是说，你应该有所准备：如果游戏发布后的收益无法解决所有问题，你该如何继续前行？如果一切结果都不如预期，你又该如何生存下去？如何在失望中，依然让团队和你保持快乐和有安全感？正当我们将注意力放在存活、创作艺术并享受生活的时候，《Pode》的销售却开始回暖。

工作的意义

2021 年，《Pode》迎来了自发布以来销量最好的一个夏天。到了 2022 年，情况更上一层楼，当我们夏季休假归来时，发现销售额已让我们成功回本，这比我们预期的更早。作为参考，过去几年《Pode》每年销量大约下降 20%，而 2022 年相比 2021 年反倒增长了 26.5%。看起来，这一增长趋势在 2023 年仍在延续。

现在我们有些困惑了，这似乎不是事情发展的正常轨迹。那么，销量为什么会持续增长呢？当然，为了提升销量，我们做了许多努力：不断推出新平台版本、举办社区活动、参加各类大会、尽可能地提供折扣，并保持线上社区的活跃度。然而，我们并未采取任何突破性举措，基本上只是稳定维护产品。因此，我们试图弄清楚这一切究竟是如何发生的。如果能总结出一套可复制的成功模式，那将对我们大有裨益。

我们得出的结论是，我们的确做出了一款优秀的游戏。这样说或许听起来有点傻气，甚至有点自夸，但我保证这才是关键所在。《Pode》拥有不错的 Metacritic 评分、正面的游戏评价、良好的玩家反馈，还拥有非常可爱的玩家社区。问题在于，如果仅以销量和盈利来衡量成功，那么以上这些价值都很容易被忽视。人们很容易放弃维护那些看似已经失败的项目，而许多优秀的游戏也正是因此被埋没。

我们都身处以将人们逼至极限而闻名的游戏行业。我们常常过于关注里程碑、发布日期和销量，却忘了当初选择进入这个行业的初衷。我们之所以能够如此鞭策自己，是因为我们对自己所做的事情充满热情。我们渴望继续做下去，渴望做得更好，渴望交出作品，渴望作品能被看见，渴望我们的艺术能被认可。我们也早已做好了为之吃苦的准备。让我们回到我妈妈的那句“艺术家也要吃饭”，以及这句话对我的意义。它让我能够停下来思考：如果我无法生存，或者如果创作的乐趣被剥夺，那么追求这些目标又有什么意义呢？

以下这些理念是我们在经营工作室时努力践行的，也希望能为大家带来一些新的思考和收获：

感谢大家。

问答环节

Q1：在积累了这些经验后，Henchman & Goon 工作室目前在做些什么？未来有哪些计划？

A1：我们目前正在推进多个项目，正努力开发其中一个主要项目，并为其争取资金支持。这个项目花费的时间比我们预期的要长，因为我们每一步都非常谨慎，避免给团队施加过多压力，尽可能保持从容的节奏。如果进度过快或遇到较大挑战，我们会暂停下来，仔细思考下一步该怎么做。


Q2：现在你知道了《Pode》的销售曲线，如果能回到游戏发布之前，你会做出哪些不同的决定？

A2：当时我们还是一个非常稚嫩的工作室，制作《Pode》是我们第一次开发如此大规模的项目，而且我们决定自发行，因此所有事情都由我们自己负责。但由于当时对游戏发行流程并不完全了解，难免会犯一些错误。回过头看，如果有机会重新选择，我们可能会考虑找一家发行商，哪怕对方不提供资金支持，至少也能帮助我们更专业地进行游戏发布，并提升知名度。毕竟，如果游戏发布时就能有更好的市场表现，即使销售曲线保持不变，整体成绩也会比现在的更理想。


Q3：你们是如何建立游戏社区的？

A3：参与游戏社区活动对我们一直非常重要，我们一直在努力结识挪威游戏社区的每一个人，并积极参加各类展会。作为开发者，在发布作品并取得一定成就后，很容易忽视那些看起来技能较低或尚未取得类似成就的人。但对我们来说，坚持不忽视任何人是至关重要的，因为你永远不知道智慧会从何而来。因此，我们欢迎每一位有兴趣参与的人，并尽可能提供帮助，无论是粉丝、玩家、学生，还是其他任何人。我们希望每个人都能参与到这段旅程中来。


Q4：你们如何在保持健康工作环境的同时，平衡摆脱合同项目的需求，尤其是在追求工作成就感的情况下？

A4：随着承接的合同项目越来越多，我们也逐渐参与到更加有趣的合作中。目前，我们正和其他游戏工作室合作开发一些很酷的项目，还和交响乐团合作，为他们的音乐会打造视觉效果。这些合作让我们的工作更加充满乐趣。因此，我认为我们的目标已经发生了变化，现在我们的目标不再是摆脱合同项目，而是找到那些最酷、最有趣的合同项目，与优秀的团队合作，共同打造令人惊叹的作品。


Q5：你们是如何与发行商建立联系，并成功获得他们的发行支持的？

A5：我们会通过多种渠道与发行商建立联系，比如发送邮件，或是在像 GDC 这样的活动中主动交流。我们尽量让自己被看见，不害羞，也不害怕被拒绝。很多人因为害怕收到负面反馈而迟迟不敢行动，但这种心理障碍才是最需要克服的。


Q6：《Pode》在发布时采用了怎样的付费广告策略？你们如今是否仍在推广这款游戏？

A6：大约在发布前六个月左右，一位投资者加入了我们，并提供了营销预算，使我们能够聘请公关公司协助推广。他们帮助我们向媒体推广，发布新闻稿等。这对我们来说很有帮助，因为如果没有这样的专业支持，我们肯定无法如此有效地触及媒体资源。

至于现在，我们依然在持续推广《Pode》。正如我之前提到的，我们采取了多种营销方式，虽然不一定是高预算的广告投放，但我们会通过折扣促销、活动推广，尽可能扩展游戏的发布平台，并尽量保持社交媒体的活跃度，以确保与玩家保持紧密联系。偶尔我们也会投放一些低预算的付费广告，虽然规模不大，但足以保持游戏销量逐渐自然增长。


Q7：相比之下，丹麦和瑞典的游戏产业似乎一直比挪威更发达。为什么会出现这种差异？如今是否有所改变？

A7：这种差异如今依然存在，挪威的游戏产业规模非常小。我不确定是否能给出确切的答案，但毫无疑问，瑞典和丹麦政府在推动本国游戏产业发展上做了大量工作。当然，近年来挪威也发生了许多有趣的变化，政府对游戏产业的关注度逐渐提升，我们已经能明显看到这些努力正在产生积极影响——挪威的游戏产业确实在增长，越来越多有趣的作品开始涌现。我希望这种差距能够逐渐缩小，但要追赶上瑞典那样的产业规模，仍然会很困难。


Q8：我来自加拿大一个游戏产业并不发达的城市。大多数人都告诉我，如果想在加拿大继续从事游戏行业，最好搬去蒙特利尔。但实际上我很希望留在自己的家乡，一个类似挪威卑尔根的小地方从事游戏工作，尽管这里并不是产业的集中地。我很好奇，你们是否也曾面临类似的挑战？此外，你们是否曾为推动当地游戏产业的发展做出贡献？

A8：是的，刚开始时确实有人问我们，为什么不去奥斯陆发展呢？那里有更大的游戏产业，离政府也更近。不过，我觉得卑尔根的人比较固执，越是有人告诉我们不应该做某事，我们反而越想去做。至于为推动本地游戏产业的发展做出贡献，首先，我们很早就聚集了卑尔根所有想在游戏行业工作的人。我们在卑尔根成立了挪威游戏开发者协会，并在当地举办了游戏大会。我们通过积极建立社区来推动这一切，这确实帮助我们吸引了更多的关注，也让更多人愿意来到卑尔根工作。所以，我认为最有效的方法就是聚集人气，建立社区，并一起做一些有趣的事情。

title: 巴士消除又爆一款，半年两款都超五千万下载，爆款休闲内购收入达2000万美金
excerpt: 同属巴士传送带消除赛道，后发的《BusFeverParty》用3个月时间把单日下载做到了对手的7倍，累计下载快速追至4500万，但IAP收入却只有对手的6%——下载量追平，商业化却差了一个量级，核心差异藏在关…
text:
文/ET
同属巴士传送带消除赛道，后发的《Bus Fever Party》用 3个月时间把单日下载做到了对手的7倍，累计下载快速追至4500万，但IAP收入却只有对手的 6%—— 下载量追平，商业化却差了一个量级，核心差异藏在关卡设计和变现体系里。
巴士消除的吸量能力还在
GOODROID旗下《Bus Traffic Fever》于今年4月份正式进入规模下载阶段，5月份起单日下载规模稳定于30-45万区间，目前双平台累计下载达到6200万次。至于Lumi Games旗下《Bus Fever Party》则是在今年8月中旬正式进入规模下载，在9月份稳定每日下载规模，每日下载量以70-80万次区间递增，双平台累计下载量超5100万次。在《Bus Fever Party》显著提升下载规模时，《Bus Traffic Fever》单日下载规模出现显著下滑，单日下载规模从45万下跌至当下10万左右，而《Bus Fever Party》每日新增下载规模依然稳定超过70万。
下载规模分布上，GOODROID旗下《Bus Traffic Fever》，安卓平台贡献4200万次下载，iOS平台贡献超2000万次下载，而Lumi Games旗下《Bus Fever Party》，安卓平台贡献超4200万次下载，iOS平台贡献接近900万次下载，安卓平台占据绝对比例。《Bus Fever Party》的单日超高下载规模，对《Bus Traffic Fever》形成巨大冲击。
地域分布上，《Bus Traffic Fever》下载区域前五地区依次为美国、墨西哥、印尼、印度、土耳其，美国占总下载规模的13%，其余四个地区合占总下载规模的25%。至于《Bus Fever Party》主要下载地区为印度、巴西、美国、墨西哥、印尼。其中，印度占总下载规模的26%，美国占总下载规模的7%。但巴西地区下载上，《Bus Fever Party》累计下载达500万次，而《Bus Traffic Fever》仅20万次。印度及巴西市场的显著下载增量，成为《Bus Fever Party》主要竞争锚点。
收入呈现差异化：新兴市场冲量，美区仍是付费核心
IAP收入方面，GOODROID旗下《Bus Traffic Fever》累计获得1900万美金IAP收入（单美国市场内购收入超1200万美金），IAP收入排名前五的国家地区分别为美国、日本、英国、加拿大、德国。其中，《Bus Traffic Fever》美国占IAP收入的63%，其余4个国家及地区合占总IAP收入的18%。至于《Bus Fever Party》，目前累计IAP流水接近150万美金，流水排名前五的国家地区分别为美国、英国、日本、澳大利亚、德国。其中，《Bus Fever Party》美国占IAP收入的68%，其余四个国家及地区合计占总IAP收入的14%。
在IAP收入的地域比例构成上，《Bus Traffic Fever》与《Bus Fever Party》十分接近。但是将这些地区的付费RPD（下载的平均收入）进行对比的话，《Bus Fever Party》与《Bus Traffic Fever》则是呈现出显著差异。印度、印尼、美国、墨西哥均为两款产品贡献较高下载的地区，但《Bus Traffic Fever》在这些地区的RPD均显著高于《Bus Fever Party》。以印度地区为例，《Bus Traffic Fever》在印度地区的RPD到达0.15美金，而《Bus Fever Party》在印度地区的RPD则不足0.01美金。随着时间的推移，尽管下载规模《Bus Fever Party》与《Bus Traffic Fever》将会到达旗鼓相当的地步，但在付费转化表现上，《Bus Fever Party》与《Bus Traffic Fever》仍存在较大的差距。
关卡路线分叉：一个走深度难度，一个走休闲爽感
事实上，《Bus Traffic Fever》在近期进行了一个显著性迭代。迭代后的《Bus Traffic Fever》游戏包体容量显著增加。
对比我们在今年6月份分析《Bus Traffic Fever》可以发现，初期游戏关卡的巴士数量显著增多，关卡采用的消除颜色数量比上一大版本游戏的数量显著提升。对应地，玩家失败概率也显著增高。交互体验上，《Bus Traffic Fever》比早期版本增加了2个隐性体验功能：巴士从操作区进入判定区以逐步放大呈现，以及游戏的“隐藏进度加速”功能。基于单关卡内容量提升，整个游戏难度上升至少1个档次。从数据表现看，这次迭代后产品的单日 IAP 收入提升近40%，道具付费渗透率显著上涨，继《Color Block Jam》及《Pixel Flow》后进一步验证了P2S（Pay to Solve）商业模式的泛用空间。除游戏难度外，包括通关道具解锁，《Bus Traffic Fever》的通关道具以2、3、5关大幅提前解锁，以实现前置商业化。
至于在《Bus Fever Party》中，大多数关卡设计分布存在间隙，巴士的朝向变得更加多元。
其次，《Bus Fever Party》初期关卡颜色数量，会显著低于《Bus Traffic Fever》。玩家在《Bus Fever Party》每进入下一关时，会出现文字提示。正常难度的关卡会提示玩家通关比例，高难度关卡则显示平均每玩家通关所需挑战次数。游戏性质上，《Bus Fever Party》定性偏向大众型休闲游戏的循序渐进设计形式，以培养用户对游戏的兴趣为基础，游戏在海外市场的下载规模得以爆发式上涨。
难度定位，决定了商业化的底层逻辑
《Bus Traffic Fever》与《Bus Fever Party》除了玩法定性的差异之外，游戏关卡设计也表现出一定程度的差异化。链路上，两款游戏均基于“传送带小人颜色分布”——“寻找操作区巴士”——“选择点击某个颜色巴士”——“查看传送带小人变化”——“点击新的巴士”。《Bus Traffic Fever》对关卡的巴士数量进行显著提升后，玩家先针对传送带其中一个颜色，找到相同颜色的巴士。《Bus Traffic Fever》关卡巴士密集分布，玩家第一次寻找的颜色巴士往往存在其他颜色巴士挡住路径，于是回到传送带查看另一个颜色，并寻找另一个颜色的巴士。期间，利用传送带入口处颜色密度，将相同颜色的小人以切割化形式展示，玩家对该颜色的巴士容量的估算受到了模糊，形成“容量>容量需求”场景，让巴士占据判定区空间。最后通过借助后续的颜色排布，形成通关失败现象。《Bus Traffic Fever》基于以高密度、大容量巴士为主的设计基调，玩家消除过程需确保判定区巴士消除之后，才进行下一次消除，行为表现以谨慎为主。
而在《Bus Fever Party》中，在关卡设计上有2个独特的细节：1、主辅色设计；2、大容量巴士比例较低。基于这两个设计，玩家处于“容量<容量需求”的场景，使消除期间需要上阵的巴士密度高。随着游戏关卡的深入，传送带面积也随之提升。此时，玩家基于传送带小人的海量，以及小型巴士作为游戏主要分布时，以非常迅速的时间即可判断点击消除。玩家在消除过程，通常采用连贯步骤的形式，达到消除连贯爽感的效果。
商业化“最后一公里”严重缺失适配性
两款产品同属混合变现赛道，最终都向 IAP 付费升级，但商业化结果天差地别，核心差异在于「难度设计与付费形式的适配度」：
《Bus Traffic Fever》：高难度 + 强卡点，道具付费是刚需，付费转化自然水涨船高；
《Bus Fever Party》：低难度 + 爽感消除，玩家靠操作就能通关，付费需求弱，只能靠广告补变现。
《Bus Traffic Fever》的商业化策略建立于游戏“以难为主”的产品基础定调上，目的为了让玩家付费成为必要性。《Bus Fever Party》由于与《Bus Traffic Fever》共同采用“左上角自动刷新重玩”这个机制，游戏自身难度大幅度降低后，重复挑战难度较低。沿用特色机制的《Bus Fever Party》，在无限制通关次数场景下，玩家重复挑战成本无限趋向于0，导致游戏内资产回收、IAA、IAP等所有商业化相对后置。
高容量巴士设定下，《Bus Traffic Fever》从初期的“单题眼”，延伸至关卡中后期的“3题眼”设定
《Bus Fever Party》难度确立与《Bus Traffic Fever》截然相反，采用相同的“重复功能”设计，反而适得其反。
对应地，玩家在《Bus Fever Party》需要增加额外判定区时，会需要触发至少2个广告点位。首先，《Bus Fever Party》基于传送带颜色及关卡排布，设立“题眼”部位，且该部位需玩家解锁超过1个额外判定区。此时，玩家陷入两个分支：
分支A：玩家每次透过IAA获得额外判定区前，都会保留1个位置，解锁后立即使用
分支B：玩家解锁1次额外判定区以后，无意间填满位置，造成通关失败
在分支A场景下，玩家每解锁1新增区域后使用1个判定区，使自身永远保持最后1个空余区域。当“题眼区”仍存在空位欠缺时，则会再次解锁额外判定区，最高单局进行4次IAA点位。原理上，借助广告观看次数成本及损失成本，最终转化IAP付费。
在分支B场景，虽然玩家同样进行IAA行为，但基于计算失误形成通关失败场景。在通关失败时，《Bus Fever Party》存在“观看广告或支付900金币，清空已被占的判定区，且额外提供1判定区”的设定。由于该设定设立1个IAA广告埋点，以1个广告点位换取3次广告权益，单难度关卡场景下玩家存在很高的转化意愿。性质上，基于“题眼”数量有限，以“题眼”的边际成本，最大化用户支出。但是，该类型的关卡数量较少，玩家感官侧无法达成“IAA支出>付费支出”，最终驱动付费转化，IAA也缺失转化次数规模。
最后，《Bus Fever Party》的主界面虽设立金币补给口如转盘、定时补给、签到等按钮，但缺少了限时多人挑战类活动场景。玩家进入游戏长留存阶段时，资产仍处于增量状态，缺乏资源投入动机。并且，对比《Bus Traffic Fever》界面设定，玩家在《Bus Fever Party》主界面无法看到显著的用户目标驱动，无法透过目标保证玩家长留存阶段的在线时长。
吸量不难，难的是商业化的精准适配
从《Color Block Jam》到《Bus Traffic Fever》，休闲消除赛道已经验证了一条规律：低难度可以快速抢量，但真正决定商业化上限的，是难度设计与付费体系的精准匹配。
《Bus Fever Party》靠轻量化难度快速吃下了下沉市场增量，证明了 “难度轻量化” 的切入路线可行，但商业化 “最后一公里” 的错配，让它空有下载量却没转化成对等的收入。反观《Bus Traffic Fever》，靠持续迭代难度、完善付费卡点，守住了收入基本盘。
对赛道厂商而言，抄玩法、抢流量不难，难的是把难度节奏、付费设计和用户画像完全对齐 —— 这才是同品类竞争里真正的护城河。 返回搜狐，查看更多

title: 前作下载过亿，收入5000万美金，这家公司却转头做了一款水排序游戏
excerpt: 换言之，它保留了水排序“顺序规划—空间约束—颜色归并—避免卡死”的核心乐趣，又用停车主题和循环机制降低了理解门槛、增强了视觉满足感。玩家不能再“想投就投”，而必须预判每一次投放会触发哪条挤出链、被挤出的车能否…
text:
虽然近几年休闲类产品出爆款的频率愈发降低，但每隔一段时间，总会出现一个新的热门玩法。三消、二合、爆破这些老品类把买量成本越推越高，旧路径对新团队来说反而越来越难走；缝隙往往出现在被低估的“小玩法”里。排序类就是这两年被重新翻出来的一条线：水排序规则直观、反馈干净，加入越来越多的新机制后，开始长出策略深度，也成为混合休闲寻找新机制时的一个方向。
上线近2个月才起量的慢热产品
近日罗斯基关注到，一款名为《Parking Loop》的产品在海外市场表现亮眼。《Parking Loop》上线于2026年9月4日，产品早期成绩并不算亮眼。在10月底开始爆发，最高排名美国App Store游戏免费榜第4。截至11月10日，《Parking Loop》依旧排在美国App Store游戏排名第18，同时在全球36个国家和地区排名免费榜Top50。
与排名相对的，《Parking Loop》的数据也在爆发式增长。据点点数据显示，在10月28日之前，《Parking Loop》单日下载量仅有1000+，28号之后开始快速增长，截至11月8日，产品最高单日下载量已突破9.3万次。
看似停车场排序，实则动态水排序
《Parking Loop》的玩法如下：屏幕上方是一个停车场，内场设有若干车位，车位上杂乱地停有大量颜色不一的汽车，外场是一圈跑道，车辆会沿跑道逆时针前进，跑道最多同时容纳5辆车。屏幕下方则是一群“嗷嗷待停”的车。
玩家点击下方小车，会将其放入跑道内。当小车首次经过相同颜色的车/空的队列，会进入车位排在其身后。这时，最下方的车会被挤出车位，在跑道中前进，寻找相同颜色的车队。当一列车位中所有小车的颜色相同，整列车会自动消除，腾出空位。当场上所有小车，以及所有“嗷嗷待停”的小车全部消除，即为关卡胜利。
试管变成队列，倒色变成投车
虽然《Parking Loop》操作简单，规则也很明了，但是想要用简短且精准的文字进行描述的话，还真有点挑战性。游戏在应用商店的副标题是“Stack Puzzle!”，即堆叠解谜。但结合玩法体验来看，这个标签并不够准确。它更像是一款披着“停车场”主题外衣的颜色排序解谜，更具体地说，是水排序玩法的一种动态化创新。停车是包装，颜色排序才是内核。
原因在于，《Parking Loop》虽然披着停车场与循环跑道的外衣，但其底层规则与水排序高度同构：颜色队列对应试管/容器，车位槽位对应容器容量，车辆颜色对应色块，点击投放对应“倒色”，队首被挤出对应“溢出转移”，整列同色消除对应“容器完成”。玩家真正要解决的，不是把车从物理空间中挪出去，而是像水排序一样，在有限空间和颜色混杂的条件下，规划每一步投放顺序，避免把队列堵死，并促成同色合并。
它的创新不在于改变水排序的“颜色归位”目标，而在于把静态试管换成了动态循环跑道：车辆不再由玩家直接倒来倒去，而是被投入跑道后自动寻找同色队列，满员后挤出队首继续流转。这使决策从“选择倒哪个容器”变为“选择投哪辆车、何时投、如何利用挤出链条”，增加了队列长度、循环相位和中转节奏的管理维度。换言之，它保留了水排序“顺序规划—空间约束—颜色归并—避免卡死”的核心乐趣，又用停车主题和循环机制降低了理解门槛、增强了视觉满足感。所以，“水排序玩法的创新”是一个比“Stack Puzzle”或单纯“停车场排序”更精准的分类。
5辆车的跑道，逼出三层难度
跑道容量为5这一约束，使游戏的难度曲线与策略深度呈现出明显层次。跑道不再是几乎无限的中转缓冲区，而是一个容量有限的调度空间。
前期颜色少、队列短时，玩家只需完成同色合并，跑道容量通常不是问题，这一阶段教的是“颜色归并”。进入中期后，随着颜色种类、待停车数量以及新机制的增加（例如未知颜色，需要放入跑道才会显现），跑道很容易接近饱和。玩家不能再“想投就投”，而必须预判每一次投放会触发哪条挤出链、被挤出的车能否在有限跑道空间内找到同色队列，以及是否为下一辆车留出周转位。这一阶段教的是“挤出链规划”。
到了后期，跑道容量会成为核心约束：投放顺序、循环相位和挤出节奏必须同时规划。跑道一满，后续车辆无法进入，关卡就可能陷入卡死。玩家不仅要考虑颜色归并，还要把跑道上的有限位置当作稀缺资源来经营：利用空位制造连续挤出，避免关键车辆占死跑道，控制同色队列的合并节奏。策略深度由此从水排序式的“顺序规划”，扩展为“顺序规划+缓冲资源管理+时机控制”。
难度曲线也因此更陡：前期教“同色归并”，中期教“挤出链规划”，后期要求“在有限跑道内完成多链协同”。每一次投放都不只是颜色决策，而是对颜色、顺序和空间的综合决策。
一个靠配对消除起家的团队，为什么转头做排序？
值得一提的是，《Parking Loop》的发行商为Loop Games Oyun Teknolojileri Anonim Sirketi（Loop Games）。
据官网资料显示，Loop Games 于2019年在土耳其安卡拉成立，不久后入选 Google 独立游戏加速器。凭借《Match 3D》和《Match Tile 3D》，开创了3D配对消除细分赛道——下载量超过1亿次，日活跃玩家达300万，收入超过5000万美元。
如果把《Parking Loop》放回 Loop Games 的产品谱系里看，它并不是一次突兀的品类跳跃。Loop Games 在自我介绍中反复强调的，是“制作让人放松的游戏”这一出发点；而他们早期在配对消除品类中验证过的，恰恰是“放松”可以通过一种非常具体的方式实现：让混乱在玩家手中被归序。
有趣的是，Loop Games 对自己游戏的描述重心并不在“匹配”这个动作上，而在关卡结束时的那个瞬间：开局时地面上散落着七八十个杂乱物件，清关后屏幕只剩一片空旷的灰色地面，这种“从满到空”的视觉对比，本身就构成了一种不需要成就徽章来提示的完成感。他们在官网博客中谈《Match 3D》时，用的词是“double the satisfaction of pairing”，把“满足感”放在了“配对”之前。
这种“满足感”的来源，并不是配对消除独有的。Loop Games后来的产品线已经延伸到排序解谜，比如《Money Sort》的核心描述就是“整理散落的钱堆，合并、排列、清出空间”。而《Parking Loop》的官方描述同样把自己定义为“a satisfying puzzle game where everything needs to find its perfect place”——关键词不是“停车”，而是“satisfying”和“perfect place”。
所以，《Parking Loop》真正从 Loop Games 那里继承的，不是“配对”这个机制外壳，而是一条更底层的产品直觉：玩家享受的，是看着一个杂乱系统在自己的操作下逐步恢复秩序，并在最后一刻被清空的那种释然。在《Match 3D》里，这种释然表现为把散落一地的物件配对拖走，露出空荡的地面；在《Parking Loop》里，它表现为把颜色混杂的车辆通过投放和挤出逐步归并，让停车场一列一列地被清空。机制从“直接配对”变成了“顺序规划下的归并”，但情绪终点是同一个：混乱被理出了头绪，空间被重新腾了出来。
配对消除和排序解谜，终点是同一个“释然”
从这个角度看，《Parking Loop》可以被视为 Loop Games 把“归序的满足感”从配对消除迁移到动态排序解谜的一次自然延伸。它蹭上的不是“配对消除”的品类标签，而是这家公司从第一天起就在经营的东西：用简单的操作，让玩家在几分钟内体验一次从无序到有序的完整释放。对于一个以“让人放松”为初衷的团队来说，这种迁移比固守一个已经成功的品类，更像他们自己会做的选择。 返回搜狐，查看更多

title: 从《燕云十六声》到六人团队，他开始做自己的动作游戏
excerpt: 凤梨罐头已经在游戏行业待了21年，从美术岗一路做到团队负责人，也曾在网易《燕云十六声》项目组担任核心职位，他对做游戏需要付出的代价有相当具体的认识。采访快结束时，凤梨罐头说，项目还需要时间，他想先把能交给玩家…
text:
这次采访刚开始，罗斯基就猜错了两次。
听说凤梨罐头离开大团队，拿自己的积蓄做单机游戏时，我们下意识地问：是不是已经实现财务自由，可以做点自己喜欢的东西了？
他赶紧否认。
换个说法，至少生活上没什么压力？他又纠正了一次：创业需要花钱，团队需要养活，他同样得考虑这些现实问题。
那么，为什么还要出来做？
“再不做的话，可能我就退休了。”
凤梨罐头已经在游戏行业待了21年，从美术岗一路做到团队负责人，也曾在网易《燕云十六声》项目组担任核心职位，他对做游戏需要付出的代价有相当具体的认识。只是，做得越久，有些念头就越难放下。
他想趁现在还有精力，把自己心里的游戏做出来。
今年5月，他在成都组起了铁凤梨工作室。算上自己，一共6个人，正在开发一款名叫《暗夜长安》的3D动作单机游戏。
唐代背景，一座发生异变的长安城，武功与志怪交织其中。光听这些关键词，容易让人联想到一个庞大的项目。但聊下来我们发现，这支团队眼下想的事情反而很具体：六个人能做好多少内容？哪些地方值得花钱？第一版战斗什么时候能交到玩家手里？
一个做了21年游戏的人重新出发时，热情仍在，账也算得更细了。
有些游戏，还是想自己做一次
凤梨罐头对动作游戏的兴趣，可以追溯到大学时期。
当时让他着迷的是《流星蝴蝶剑》。人物能在三维空间里腾挪，轻功和兵器交锋带来的自由感，让他第一次对“自己做这样的游戏”产生了强烈兴趣。后来，他真的进入了昱泉。
多年以后，吸引他加入《燕云十六声》的，同样是玩游戏时的感受。
他会留意场景的空间比例，也会被支线里的文字和人物打动。在他看来，有些内容能让玩家感觉到，背后有人认真琢磨过。对一个长期从事美术工作的人来说，看到喜欢的东西，就想参与进去，看看它究竟是怎样做出来的。
不过，参与大项目和自己做主，终究是两种不同的经历。
大型团队要协调很多人的目标，一个决定落下去，牵涉的是制作成本、开发进度，以及不同环节的需求。凤梨罐头理解这些取舍，也做过类似的管理工作。但理解归理解，他仍然有一些想按自己方式完成的表达。
此前的项目经历，也让他更在意一件事——希望有机会把一款作品持续做下去，听到玩家的反馈，再亲手把它改好。
聊到这种心情时，他说：
“要是你试都不试的话，那这个不甘心它就会变成一个永久的东西，你永远都会不甘心。”
于是，他拿出积蓄，找来几位愿意同行的伙伴，开始做《暗夜长安》。
这次创业没有多少豪言壮语。他知道自己的钱能承担多少，也知道现阶段的团队能做到什么程度。真正推动他迈出这一步的，是一个放了很多年，至今还想实现的念头。
六个人的长安，得从每一场战斗做起
《暗夜长安》的故事发生在一座陷入异变的古城里。玩家进入这座城市，探索街巷，遭遇敌人，逐渐弄清它为什么变成了现在的样子。
团队希望把唐代城市的风貌与东方志怪结合起来，让武功、怪物和法术共同构成游戏的战斗体验。凤梨罐头不太愿意过早给它贴上“魂类”的标签。现阶段，他更看重动作本身的体验，也想给设计留出空间，不必被某种既有类型的难度和关卡惯例框住。
当然，六个人做3D动作游戏，规模是绕不开的问题。
采访中，我们提到“2A”，他觉得这个说法可能仍然偏大，开玩笑说，自己的项目也许只能算“N分之一A”。如果预算充足，他当然也想做更大的游戏。但现在，每增加一块内容，都要考虑谁来做、做多久，以及后面需要多少调整。
因此，《暗夜长安》选择先围绕一座相对紧凑的箱庭城市展开。
古城本身就有适合关卡设计的结构。城门与围墙可以划分区域，河流和桥梁能够组织路线，不同街区再通过通道连接起来。团队也在考虑地下空间，以及城外的山地、峡谷，让探索有更多高低变化。
至少从目前的思路看，他们希望把有限的内容做得更集中，让玩家在一座城里找到足够多值得探索的地方。
美术是凤梨罐头熟悉的领域。多年经验让他知道，一个画面效果需要哪些工序，质量差距出在哪里，又会花掉多少时间。但到了自己负责整个项目时，他也必须控制美术投入，给性能优化和玩法留出资源。
尤其是动作游戏，漂亮的截图很难替代上手之后的感受。因此团队眼下把优先级放在核心战斗上。先做出能玩的版本，让核心玩家试，再根据反馈调整。
AI进了工作流，经验依然很值钱
六个人敢尝试这样的项目，新工具确实给了他们一些底气。
铁凤梨工作室已经在程序和美术环节使用AI，包括辅助编程、概念探索、模型生成，以及部分场景制作流程。团队里年轻成员上手很快，凤梨罐头自己也在不断测试这些工具能解决什么问题。
聊到这里，他的一个判断是：“会手搓才能用好AI。”
一张概念图看起来不错，接下来还得判断，它是否符合项目的美术方向，能否转成可用的资产。生成的模型进入游戏，也需要检查和修改。熟悉制作流程的人，知道哪些结果可以接着用，哪些问题必须推倒重来，才能把工具省下来的时间真正留下。
对他而言，AI最有价值的地方，是让有经验的人少做一些重复劳动，把精力放到判断和调整上。过去积累的能力，也因此有了新的用法。
但动作游戏里还有不少硬骨头。
例如动画和特效，最终要进入引擎，与角色状态、战斗逻辑配合。生成一段看起来流畅的视频，和做出游戏里能准确响应操作的动作资源，制作要求差别很大。这些环节仍然需要大量人工处理，也是团队当前要承担的成本。
所以，AI进入工作流之后，《暗夜长安》依然得认真控制规模。
回到熟悉的地方，和愿意同行的人一起做
凤梨罐头工作室放在成都，有很朴素的原因。
这里是凤梨罐头熟悉的生活环境，有家人，也有固定一起踢球的朋友。创业已经带来足够多的变化，他希望生活能保留一些熟悉的节奏。当地的成本，也更适合现阶段的团队。
现在，他们通常上午10点开始工作，晚上8点左右结束，周六也会继续做项目。
团队的组成，同样依靠多年积累的关系与信任。有老伙伴愿意再一起试一次，也有人需要更稳定的收入，选择了其他工作。凤梨罐头理解这些决定。每个人都有家庭和各自的安排，创业很难要求所有人承担同样的风险。
资金仍然是现实课题。尤其进入美术内容的集中制作阶段后，投入会继续增加。团队在寻找合适的支持，也考虑过通过其他项目获得收入，维持开发。无论如何，他们现在最需要拿出来的，仍然是一款能够让人上手的游戏。
采访快结束时，凤梨罐头说，项目还需要时间，他想先把能交给玩家体验的版本做好。等战斗得到反馈，再逐步补齐内容和表现，给大家看一个更完整的《暗夜长安》。
他面对具体问题时的那股认真劲儿，让罗斯基印象深刻：做了21年游戏，他依然愿意亲自下场，把这些问题重新解一遍。
《暗夜长安》的第一批玩家，或许很快就会成为这场尝试的一部分。 返回搜狐，查看更多

title: 玩家追着广告点歌，这款小游戏把买量做出了新花样
excerpt: 用户在意谁、想看什么，可以直接成为下一条素材的线索，而角色兴趣又能接回游戏。这样的反馈，让发行团队看到了持续经营内容的意义——每一条视频都可以为下一次接触增加一点熟悉感。围绕视频号、游戏圈和公众号的联动，团队…
text:
做游戏广告，被用户催更是什么体验？
《永夜起源》的团队遇到了。评论区里，有人指定下一条视频出哪个角色，有人给角色点歌，还有人看完剧情后建议他们干脆去做短剧，自己一定付费支持。
对于做了多年买量的项目发行负责人刘毅来说，这样的反馈也是第一次见。用户因为广告关注官方账号，追着看后续内容，甚至留言说看了这么多期，决定进游戏体验一下。
根据刘毅在采访中的介绍，团队在视频号单条视频的最高播放量达到700万；做出内容向素材之后，视频号的加热消耗规模扩大至上线初期的5—6倍，产品本身最高登上微信小游戏畅销榜第四。
对一家成立两年多、不到40人的发行公司而言，《永夜起源》是一次重要的起步。它也提供了一个有意思的样本：
当用户愿意追着广告看，小游戏发行可以玩出什么花样？
让唐僧唱歌，想卖的依然是那张卡
《永夜起源》主打西游题材的抽卡养成和放置推图。团队选择这个方向，首先考虑的就是认知门槛。
用户一眼便能理解世界观，接下来再用角色设计制造记忆点。比如传统印象里的唐僧文弱、手无缚鸡之力，《永夜起源》把他做成了肌肉线条硬朗的威猛形象。熟悉的人物与反差外形结合，用户很快就能记住。
另一个超出团队预期的角色是大黑天。这个偏御姐风格的角色受到玩家欢迎，有人直接在素材评论区点名，希望她出镜。
刘毅反复提到一个判断——卡牌游戏的核心卖点，就是角色本身。
发行初期，团队便在讨论，除了立绘和技能特效，还有什么办法能让玩家喜欢一个角色？西游天然带有群像特点，每个人物都可以有自己的性格和表达。唱歌、跳舞和剧情，恰好能把游戏画面之外的那部分魅力补出来。
最先获得良好反馈的，是一条唐僧唱歌的视频。歌曲与角色声线、形象比较契合，评论区很快热闹起来。有人觉得唐僧的声音冷酷，还希望他尝试摇滚。
这给团队带来了新的创作方向。
用户在意谁、想看什么，可以直接成为下一条素材的线索，而角色兴趣又能接回游戏。用户被唐僧吸引，进入游戏后确实可以获得这个角色，前期体验中也能用得上。
用户从喜欢一个角色，到想把他收入卡组，这段距离其实比想象中短。这也是唱歌素材能够服务卡牌商业化的原因。内容让角色变得鲜活，游戏则给玩家提供了收集和培养角色的空间。
AI打开了表达空间，团队提前练好了手艺
让游戏角色唱歌，听起来像是一个赶上热点的创意。真正做起来，背后仍然是一套细致的内容工作。
团队会先确定角色人设，判断适合什么剧情、什么曲风，再搭出创意框架。做原创歌曲时，他们自己研究歌词内容，然后借助AI完善韵脚和旋律，从中选择适合角色的版本。视频也需要拆分镜，逐段生成，再完成拼接和衔接。画面要求复杂的脚本，一天未必能做完。
AI带来的提升，在一些高制作要求的内容上尤其明显。按刘毅的经验，过去某类战斗画面一个月只能产出一两条，如今借助AI，一两天便有机会完成。
不过，《永夜起源》并非团队接触AI的起点。今年年初，视频和图片生成模型快速发展时，他们就开始投入。当时运营的产品收入有限，工具费用也不低，生成素材的回收尚未达到预期，团队依然持续打磨工作流程。
等到《永夜起源》上线，这些积累有了发挥的地方。
设计人员的培养也跟着变化。团队要求AI进入从提示词优化到画面产出的工作过程，并把优秀同事的做法推广给其他人，让制作能力逐渐稳定下来。
刘毅承认，他们抓住了一段创意方向的先行窗口。与此同时，同样的脚本交给不同设计师，审美、提示词和成片质量仍然会拉开差距。
700万播放之后，视频号加热进一步放大生意
内容获得关注后，还需要让它持续触达用户，并把兴趣引向游戏。
《永夜起源》从首发阶段就同步使用视频号加热和腾讯营销投放管理平台（ADQ）。早期素材偏向传统游戏硬广，后续内容向创意跑出来，消耗规模随之扩大。
刘毅表示，“视频号矩阵+加热”对产品流水的贡献正在增加。视频号加热和腾讯营销投放的加持，让这套内容做法有了持续放大的条件。团队仍按效果广告的方式观察回收，表现好就增加投入，再沿着有效方向迭代创意。
素材测试中，他们也积累了一些经验。
有的视频刚上传、尚未加热，自然播放就明显高于其他内容，这类素材往往更容易起量。还有一些素材，初期曝光有限，过一段时间重新加热，却能跑出不错的效果。因此，团队会反复使用优质内容，也会定期重测历史素材。
更有意思的变化，发生在单次投放之外。部分用户看完广告没有立刻进游戏，却关注了账号。后续视频继续触达，他们开始熟悉角色、参与评论，甚至主动等待更新。团队因此攒下了一批对产品有兴趣的潜在玩家。
刘毅记得，有用户留言表示，广告越做越好，自己要去支持一下。这样的反馈，让发行团队看到了持续经营内容的意义——每一条视频都可以为下一次接触增加一点熟悉感。
唐僧的投放表现优于其他男角色，团队便据此讨论后续男性角色的设计方向；哪些女性角色受欢迎，也会被带进与研发的沟通。
广告逐渐成为团队了解用户、完善角色的一扇窗口。
当广告有人追更，角色就值得长期经营
目前，《永夜起源》团队已经运营五六个视频号账号，希望逐步形成内容分工。喜欢听歌的人能找到唱歌内容，想看剧情的人也有相应账号可追。
围绕视频号、游戏圈和公众号的联动，团队还在继续探索，因为小游戏除了转化链路短的优势以外，内容体验与社区交流可以在同一生态中连接，为产品长线运营留下空间。角色受到欢迎之后，团队甚至考虑在合适的节点制作手办或道具周边，回馈用户。
对于一家以发行起步的小公司，这已经打开了新的想象。
《永夜起源》的案例给罗斯基的一个感受是：小游戏团队手里的角色资产，还有不少可挖掘的价值。
玩家既可以在抽卡界面认识角色，也可以先通过一首歌或者一段剧情喜欢上他。AI让这些表达更容易实现，视频号提供了内容被发现和持续更新的场景。商业化一侧，加热工具将有效创意推向更大的人群，小游戏负责承接随之而来的参与欲。
这套做法能跑通，其实是团队愿意认真回答一个问题：除了展示玩法，我们的角色还有什么值得用户喜欢？
当答案足够有趣，评论区就会变成点歌和催更，而不是问“这个游戏是否逼氪”。
对游戏公司而言，这样的兴趣，值得花时间经营下去。 返回搜狐，查看更多

title: OpenAI亲自下场做游戏了
excerpt: 它能让用户通过Codex制作游戏，再把作品写入卡带，带出门去玩。关于AI做游戏，行业已经讨论了很多技术进步；这次，OpenAI试着给普通玩家一个更具体的理由：按照OpenAI官方教程，用户可以向Codex描述…
text:
小时候玩Game Boy时你有没有想过，往卡槽里插一张自己做的游戏？
OpenAI把这个念头做成了一门售价200美元的生意。
最近，OpenAI旗下商店Supply Co.上架了ModRetro Chromatic的Codex联名版。这台掌机有透明外壳、实体按键和小小的彩色屏幕，还保留了插卡带的玩法。它能让用户通过Codex制作游戏，再把作品写入卡带，带出门去玩。
最新的AI编程工具，配上一套几十年前就让玩家着迷的游戏体验，确实是一个很有噱头的组合。关于AI做游戏，行业已经讨论了很多技术进步；这次，OpenAI试着给普通玩家一个更具体的理由：
做一张属于自己的游戏卡带。
200美元买一台掌机，也买一个动手的理由
Chromatic来自复古硬件厂商ModRetro，OpenAI参与的是联名合作，以及Codex与开发工具的连接。产品最初以DevDay限定形式亮相，如今换上新外观，进入Supply Co.销售。
它的硬件规格很有年代感：2.56英寸屏幕，160×144分辨率，使用三节AA电池，也兼容充电电源配件。掌机支持Game Boy、Game Boy Color和Chromatic游戏卡带，200美元的套装里附带一张可编程卡带。
AI发挥作用的地方在电脑端。用户通过Codex完成游戏创作，得到ROM文件，便能将作品写入卡带，在掌机上独立运行。
这件事的吸引力，其实很难用开发效率解释。浏览器里的小游戏可以随手关闭，一张由自己制作的卡带却很适合收藏把玩，甚至送给朋友。
ModRetro本身也在经营这样的创作文化。早在2024年，公司就公开招募独立开发者为Chromatic制作新游戏，并强调实体卡带发行。OpenAI加入之后，这个原本偏向开发者和复古爱好者的领域，多了一条面向普通用户的入口。
一句话，生成一张可以玩的卡带
这套体验的关键，是ModRetro Chromatic插件。
按照OpenAI官方教程，用户可以向Codex描述想做的游戏，让它生成项目并打开模拟器预览。随后继续提出修改要求，最终编译出适用于Game Boy Color的游戏文件。
教程展示的《Lodge Podge》里，玩家控制一只像素海狸，收集树枝建造自己的窝。开发过程中，创作者又要求加入泥土和树叶，丰富资源收集，同时把海狸改得更胖一些。
插件还提供了在暂停画面上选中对象、描述修改需求的方式，并能让Codex执行按键序列，截图检查运行结果。项目可以继续在GB Studio中人工编辑，完成后再编译和烧录。
OpenAI也准备了作品展示页面，目前列出13款使用Codex为Game Boy Color制作的游戏，包括《FlapGPT》《Codex Land》《Hollow Descent》和《Pizza Dash》等。用户可以在浏览器里游玩，也可以下载ROM，在兼容设备上运行。
AI为什么和复古游戏凑到了一起？
乍看之下，这个选择有些跳脱，像是搞怪整活儿。但从创作体验看，小屏幕恰好给了用户一个清楚的起点。
你很容易想象一只角色在房间里走动，收集几个道具，打开一扇门。这样的目标足够小，修改结果又足够直观。一次迭代之后，用户很快就能看到自己的想法有没有奏效。如果一开始就把目标设为宏大的开放世界，创作者容易被不断膨胀的需求拖住。
复古游戏的规格，天然收紧了范围。有限的画面和操作，也会推动人把注意力放到规则本身。
OpenAI此前已经尝试过类似的体验。
在2025年DevDay官方复盘中，公司介绍了现场的两台ArcadeGPT街机。参与者可以通过GPT-5改编现有游戏。为了准备基础内容，开发者Kevin Whinnery曾同时开启七个Codex CLI实例，制作不同的Phaser游戏。
现场街机让人体验修改游戏的乐趣，掌机卡带则把成果交到用户手里。两者回答的其实同一个问题——怎样让更多人愿意迈出做游戏的第一步？
有些人做游戏，就是为了好玩
讨论AI游戏创作时，游戏行业喜欢直接跳到商业问题：能否替代岗位，能否出爆款，能否建立新的内容平台。
这台掌机提供了另一组更贴近日常的场景。
有人可能想给朋友做一段只有彼此才能看懂的小冒险，有人想把宠物画成主角，也有人（比如主播和Up主）会将制作过程拍成视频，把观众的建议加进下一版游戏。实体卡带给这段过程增加了一个明确的终点。
对游戏行业而言，这种需求值得关注。面向普通用户的创作工具，可以围绕小型作品设计模板和编辑流程。创作过程本身，则能成为视频、直播和线下活动的一部分。
过去，我们插进卡槽的游戏，大多来自某个遥远的开发团队。
现在，有人希望下一张卡带，来自玩家自己。 返回搜狐，查看更多

title: 'Season 10 has been a challenging one for us': Marvel Rivals is upgrading Storm's summer skin after favouritism complaints
author: Elie Gould
text:
Skin distribution seems to be an issue in pretty much any game with more than one hero and clear favourites. Marvel Rivals has come under fire for it for a while now, ever since players got wise to which heroes were favourites and which had clearly been shoved to the side.
It all came to a head a few months ago when the summer skins were released, and it was revealed that Storm was the only female hero to not get a legendary costume among all the swimsuit designs. Players did not look upon this favourably , as Storm is a hugely popular character and had already gone a long time without the same kind of legendary skins as other heroes like Luna Snow and had been passed over for skins in the Disco and Egyptian God skin lines.
(Image credit: NetEase) But all the player complaints seem to have gotten through to NetEase, with creative director Guangyun Chen acknowledging in a dev diary that "season 10 has been a challenging one for us." Not only were players upset about only one hero being released this season, but the devs have "been closely following the community's feedback regarding certain heroes receiving fewer costumes. With strong demands for more high-quality Legendary costumes featuring recolours and ultimate ability visual upgrades."
The decision has since been made to upgrade Storm's summer skin to legendary tier with the devs "targeting a release around Christmas this December" for it. Other slightly forgotten heroes who will be getting some visual upgrades include Human Torch, who will get a legendary costume in early December which includes "recolours and ultimate ability VFX". Cloak and Dagger will also be getting a (presumably Valentines Day-themed) skin in February.
"We've been hard at work at this for almost eight months," Guangyun Chen says. "Cloak's design will include full legs. We fully re-animated Cloak's entire movement set strictly for this, we really hope you enjoy it."
But with all these new redesigns and costumes on the way, Guangyun Chen wants to remind players that skins can't just be made or changed at a moment's notice: "Please understand that art asset production requires a certain lead time and simply can't be done overnight. Generally, a single costume takes eight to 10 months to produce from start to finish."
Storm's redesigned summer skin has been in the works for three months already, with the finished product coming out after five months of work. That's under the average of eight to 10 months, but this sounds like the exception not the rule.

title: 22 years after the Hot Coffee controversy, UK politician says Grand Theft Auto 6 is 'something that we can be really proud of'
author: Andy Chalk
text:
It's fascinating how things change. I. for instance, used to love staying up all night playing videogames; now I get mad at the world if I miss my bedtime by 10 minutes. In kind of a similar vein, Grand Theft Auto was once the poster child for everything insidious, dangerous, and downright wrong about videogames, but now we have a member of the UK government—a secretary of state, no less—talking about how the upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6 is something the whole country should be proud of.
"My love for videogames knows no bounds, and I am an avid addict of things like Animal Crossing and the Mario series," Lisa Nandy, the UK's secretary of state for digital, culture, media, and sport, told The Rundown. "I'm not sure I get away with taking a day off to do it, but I think it's something that we can be really proud of.
"One of the reasons that we're investing in arts and music and all of those things that give people the chance to live richer, larger lives is because we are creating jobs in these incredible industries. And if you want to make a videogame like Grand Theft Auto, you need animators, you need musicians, you need so many people from across the creative industries to make them work. And why shouldn't it be our children in our communities who get the chance to get those jobs?"
I'm as politically cynical as most folks, and sure, Nandy is using the moment opportunistically to promote her government—although, cynicism notwithstanding, I do respect her ability to stay on-message by turning a softball question about GTA 6 into talking about job creation.
At the same time, though, this is a remarkable turnaround from, say, 20 years ago, when everyone in a position of authority lost their minds over the Hot Coffee mod for GTA: San Andreas. Some of you might not be old enough to remember (you have no idea how much it pains me to say that) but referring to GTA as a legitimate cultural export in the early 2000s would've got any mainstream Western politician laughed out of the room—and suggesting that it'd be cool if the children ( the children! ) grew up to make more games like that? Pure political suicide.
As PC Gamer's Evan Lahti wrote in 2017 , "Any American who played games in the '90s remembers the period of pearl-clutching and pseudoscientific fear-mongering from senators like Joe Lieberman, who led a call to ban violent videogames." This was serious stuff back then, and it wasn't really until the US Supreme Court ruled that videogames, like other creative works, are protected speech under the First Amendment that the hysteria and hand-wringing started to meaningfully die down.
But now here we are, 15 years later: The Miami Heat are cosplaying as a Vice City sports team , Rockstar is holding a huge GTA music festival featuring Cardi B and Travis Scott , half the state of Florida is embracing a Leonida transformation (and the cops aren't even mad about it ), and now we've got the UK government saying it's all quite grand— splendid , even. Time, man. It really is a river carving the bedrock of our souls.

title: Overwatch's creative director accidentally leaks the name of season 6's upcoming hero and reveals that he 'got the highest scores of any hero that we've tested'
author: Elie Gould
text:
Earlier this year, during the Overwatch Spotlight in which Team 4 promised a different approach to managing the live service game, 10 heroes were teased. Five were released straight away , with Sierra, Shion, D.Mon, and Doctrine all being added to the game in subsequent seasons. This has left just one hero for the last season of the year, who also just so happened to be the hero I was most excited about back when the Spotlight was released.
But good things come to those who wait, and now after the better part of a year we finally know more about this final hero. His character design was shown at BlizzCon, which showed him to be omnic detective (my hype was well placed), but now we also know that he'll be joining the DPS class in season 6, although that wasn't always the plan.
(Image credit: Blizzard Entertainment) "Back at Spotlight—I forget who I was talking to—we said we were going to do a support in season 6," associate game director Alec Dawson said during a stream with Flats and Emongg . "And originally that was the plan. But as things developed as the hero developed, as we got to mechanics, how they matched with the aesthetic, how they matched with who the hero is supposed to be," things changed. The decision was ultimately taken to switch him to the DPS role. "I don't know what else I'm allowed to say," Dawson adds. "I'll let Aaron [Keller, game director] say anything else."
"We'll just spill it all," Keller says, and that he does. "Megan just slacked that we've said enough but there's a couple of other things that I want to say about him. One of the cool things about this, so there was like a bit of a pivot on Hudson (accidentally leaks his name), oh whoops." Well there it is folks: the omnic detective is called Hudson, a cool name for a cool dude, it all checks out.
Hudson's Role Change Explained in #Overwatch 🔎He was initially planned as a Support hero, but as development progressed, the team realized the core mechanic people loved most fit the DPS role better.The hero set record scores in research groups. https://t.co/VxTMpsPLUr November 13, 2026
As a support main I am a little sad to hear about this change to DPS, but seeing as Team 4 explained how they "leaned into the things we loved the most about this hero and it definitely fit DPS a lot better", I'm happy with the change. I'll just have to put support aside for a couple of months, because there's no way I'm missing out on this hero.
This isn't just because he looks cool; according to Keller, Hudson is the most popular hero to-date among their internal and external testers: "We're always testing stuff and we have a user research group here and we'll bring in external players and stuff like that, and this hero by far got the highest scores of any hero that we've tested with these groups. I think he's so much fun."
To put this into perspective, the second most popular hero among testers within the last few years is Juno; a hero I would consider to be one of the best in recent Overwatch history. Her kit is fun, intuitive, and gels with her character design. So if that's the bar Hudson has beaten then my excitement is yet again very well placed. Oh, and Dawson says "he has a very fun accent", which really seals the deal for me.

title: 8BitDo Ultimate 3E wireless controller review
author: James Bentley
text:
Pricing has remained the elephant in the room for almost all PC Gaming hardware this year, but when it comes to controllers, you don't even have the memory crisis to blame.
And yet, I feel similarly about the 8BitDo Ultimate 3E as I do all that memory-equipped hardware: This is genuinely an excellent gamepad that I have loved reaching for every day, but that price stings so badly that it becomes quite hard to recommend.
Unless, of course, you really want a dual-compatible (Xbox and PC) modular wireless controller.
Buy if…
✅ You want the best wireless pad for your Xbox: The Ultimate 3E acts exactly like the standard Microsoft Xbox controller, even waking up the console with the on button, except it's better in almost every way.
Don't buy if…
❌ You want the best value for money: You can get the GameSir G7 Pro, with its tri-mode connectivity and charging stand for nearly half the price. Add ten bucks to the G7 Pro, and you can even get its 8K variant.
Features
8BitDo Ultimate 3E specs Layout
Asymmetrical
Thumbsticks
TMR
Gyro
6-axis gyroscope
Connectivity
Tri-mode for PC and Xbox. Bluetooth for Mobile
Battery
1400 mAh, 18-hour playtime
Polling Rate
1,000 Hz (250 Hz on Xbox)
Dimensions
152.5 x 104 x 62 mm
Weight
285 g
Price
$150 / £140
This isn't just a PC controller that works wired on an Xbox, like most controllers. This is an officially licensed product with Microsoft's coveted wireless chip inside, meaning it works wirelessly on Xbox and PC. Not only that, but it even wakes up the Xbox when you click the On button, effectively doing what the standard Xbox controller does. This may not seem like a big deal, but it's shockingly rare among third-party controller manufacturers right now.
To swap between PC and Xbox, you just have to swap the adapter between the two. Given the price, I'd really love two adapters, as the Turtle Beach Stealth Pro II has, but it's not a huge pain, and the controller has Bluetooth and wired connectivity.
In addition to coming with a charging dock, carry case, and USB Type-A to Type-C cable, the case comes with spare thumbsticks, face buttons, and a D-pad. That's because the Ultimate 3E is modular. You can take off the faceplate and swap around the parts above in mere moments. It's intuitive, and all the parts are built well.
Future Future You also get more modern controller upgrades, like TMR joysticks, two buttons at the back and two extra buttons on top. It does do away with some of my criticisms of the 8BitDo Pro 3 by giving you a 1,000 Hz polling rate and an aux jack, but even then, I would have hoped for 8,000 Hz at this price point. Admittedly, most players won't use 8,000 Hz polling given its battery-sucking ways, but you'd still expect a pro-level controller to have everything thrown at it.
The main difference between the Ultimate 3 and Ultimate 3E is that the 3E comes with RGB rings around the sticks, has rubberised grips at the front and back, and, of course, modular parts. The 3E is also heavier.
Future Future Future As far as modularity is concerned, it's very easy to do. For the thumbsticks and D-pad, you can simply pull them until they pop off, and then slot in the replacement. The face buttons are a little more involved, with you needing to take the faceplate off, pinch the two sides of the face button module and pull. From here, you can swap with the included face button module in the carry case, which is identical except it comes with mechanical switches.
It seems unlikely you will use this modularity every day, but this level of customisation is certainly welcome to me, and does make the controller feel unique. Unfortunately, though, it doesn't opt for any peculiar modules, like the Victrix Pro BFG Reloaded , which does feel like a slightly wasted opportunity.
Given it works on PC and Xbox, I'd love a touchpad module option. The Victrix even gives you the option to change the stick layout, which the Ultimate 3E doesn't. There are levels of modularity on controllers, and the Pro BFG Reloaded is one level above.
Ergonomics
At 285 grams, the 8BitDo Ultimate 3E is around 10 grams lighter than the standard Xbox controller, and it feels super sturdy and comfortable in the hands. The Ultimate 3 and 3E are slightly larger than the Ultimate 2, and I can comfortably say this is the sweetest 8BitDo controller I've held. It's impeccably well-balanced and smoothly slots into my palms. All of its buttons are easy to get to, and surprisingly, I even found myself using the two extra buttons near the bumpers. 8BitDo clearly knows how to make a great-feeling controller.
If I really shake it, the controller has a slight rattle in the centre, but I never heard that in the course of usual play.
Future Future Future Future The Ultimate 3E has been my pad of choice whilst trying to collect the Fortnite Pirate Token, and I may not have gotten the loot, but I have managed to achieve a tonne of kills. It's not failed me once in its connectivity; buttons are snappy and precise, and it doesn't fatigue me after hours of bad luck in the game.
More recently, it's been my way of playing Warhammer Survivors , a very chill game where you constantly hold down the thumbsticks, and these TMR sticks are impressive—precise and smooth.
Aesthetics
Future Future Future Future The best word I can use to describe the Ultimate 3E is clean. Well, not after my hands get on it, but we'll get to that later. The 3E comes in a suave black model, with almost every element of the pad being a shade of black. The only thing cutting through that lack of colour is the LED around the on button and the RGB sticks. Simply click the start button to turn on the RGB, and hold it while using the D-pad to change colour, vibrancy and mode.
It reminds me of a souped-up version of Nintendo's Pro Controller, and that is a big compliment in my eyes. The Ultimate 3 does have some gorgeous colourways, but if you want something simple yet pretty, the 3E is great.
The same can be said for the stand, which is all black with a small RGB strip which doubles as a way of telling you if your controller is charging.
However, there is one blemish here: the grips can get grubby. I've been using GameSir's G7 Pro 8K for almost half a year now and I haven't managed to get its grips quite as mucky looking at the 3E. It certainly doesn't look awful with a speck of dust or grime on the grip, but it does look less clean in both senses of the word.
Software
(Image credit: 8BitDo) For the Ultimate 3E, 8BitDo uses the Ultimate Software X, which is the same software it uses for Xbox devices. This is mildly annoying as I use the standard Ultimate software for my Retro keyboard and Retro R8 gaming mouse, meaning I can't use one bit of software for all three.
With this software, you can customise the range and rumble of the triggers, the deadzone of sticks, and get firmware updates. It's fairly straightforward, though after the initial setup, you can do most of the everyday customising without software, including setting controls to the extra buttons, adjusting RGB, and even changing volume.
Battery Life
8BitDo Ultimate 3E next to the Xbox controller (Image credit: Future) The 1400 mAh battery gets around 18 hours of play before it needs to charge again. That's fine. It's not especially big, but it's not minuscule either. However, I have never once needed to consciously charge the controller, because the stand is just the natural place I'd put the controller at the end of the day. The stand looks pretty, and I've never managed to place it at such an odd angle that the controller won't charge. I have, on many occasions, very haphazardly slotted it on top, and it's been ready to go the next day.
The benefit of this charging stand is that it has a hidden compartment underneath to slot the 2.4 GHz connector, meaning it works as both a charging stand and receiver.
Value
(Image credit: Future) If you are looking for something like the Xbox Elite Controller that works wirelessly on Xbox, the Ultimate 3E is basically 8BitDo's imitation, but cheaper. And that seems to be the main sell, here.
However, if you are simply looking for a great wireless controller for your PC with solid specs and a great feel, it's significantly more expensive than the comparably good GameSir G7 Pro . In fact, the GameSir G7 Pro 8K even outpaces it for PC competitive performance thanks to a polling rate that is eight times higher.
As such, there's only one specific niche for which I could wholeheartedly recommend the Ultimate 3E, and that's if you are primarily an Xbox gamer in need of a wireless controller. But for the average PC Gamer, the Ultimate 3E, even with its neat modular functions and sweet feel, is $50 more than I'd happily pay.
One thing I can say is that it has replaced every other controller when it comes to my Xbox, and that is somewhat of a win for 8BitDo, even if it feels like a begrudging one at $150.

title: I cannot stop everyone staring at me in GTA 5
author: Joshua Wolens
text:
Los Santos Customs
I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .
As we've covered in previous lectures, everyone is Franklin . This is disconcerting. Even more disconcerting is that, as of today, all the Franklins now have a singular object of cathexis: Franklin.
Uh, that is to say, Franklin Prime: me. I have installed Look At Me , a Grand Theft Auto 5 mod whose purpose is to make you the centre of attention wherever you go and wherever you teleport. In the street, crowds round on you, fixing you with a silent stare as though they know everything you've ever done, everything you will ever do. Even parkour does not mollify them.
(Image credit: Rockstar) It turns your every step in GTA 5 into something paranoid and faintly Lynchian. I am being gangstalked by myself, and all the while wars rage, cars float overhead, and the world in general spins out of control on every axis. Sometimes it finds new axes, and they're all irreparably hosed.
Look At Me does not appear to affect NPCs who have been placed with a purpose. Or it sometimes doesn't, anyway. My bodyguard? Unpredictable. Sometimes he will stand stock-still, and join the masses in gawping at me. Other times, he couldn't care less. My wife never looks at me; this is troubling.
It's a bold and unnerving new world, and one that I suppose is much harder to commit unwitnessed crimes in. Does anyone know how to make my wife look at me again? Taking suggestions.

Los Santos Customs

I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.

As we've covered in previous lectures, everyone is Franklin. This is disconcerting. Even more disconcerting is that, as of today, all the Franklins now have a singular object of cathexis: Franklin.

Uh, that is to say, Franklin Prime: me. I have installed Look At Me, a Grand Theft Auto 5 mod whose purpose is to make you the centre of attention wherever you go and wherever you teleport. In the street, crowds round on you, fixing you with a silent stare as though they know everything you've ever done, everything you will ever do. Even parkour does not mollify them.

It turns your every step in GTA 5 into something paranoid and faintly Lynchian. I am being gangstalked by myself, and all the while wars rage, cars float overhead, and the world in general spins out of control on every axis. Sometimes it finds new axes, and they're all irreparably hosed.

Look At Me does not appear to affect NPCs who have been placed with a purpose. Or it sometimes doesn't, anyway. My bodyguard? Unpredictable. Sometimes he will stand stock-still, and join the masses in gawping at me. Other times, he couldn't care less. My wife never looks at me; this is troubling.

It's a bold and unnerving new world, and one that I suppose is much harder to commit unwitnessed crimes in. Does anyone know how to make my wife look at me again? Taking suggestions.

title: New Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer is for a TV show that exists within Grand Theft Auto 6
author: Andy Chalk
text:
Get ready for some wheels within wheels, as DiscussingFilm has revealed an animated trailer for a Grand Theft Auto 6 TV show—and I don't mean a trailer for a show about GTA 6, but a trailer for a show in GTA 6.
Macca and Friends, as the show is known, follows the adventures of a gang of anthropomorphic Floridian—Leonidan, I suppose—animals as they try to find their way in the world, accompanied to some extent by a beefed-up cop. The animals are cops too. It's a bit like Scooby Doo, maybe, but more egalitarian.
Rockstar hasn't said anything about the show, but this isn't the first appearance of Macca: A Macca and Friends mural appeared in a real-life BurgerShot that was set up in Miami's Kaseya Center in October, and a billboard for the show was erected in Miami as well.
Both advertised Macca and Friends as "coming November 19 on Weazel," a Fox-like television channel that exists within the GTA universe.
Rockstar is now marketing GTA 6 with a real-life Burger Shot food stand in Kaseya Center, Miami.They continue preparing for the major Miami Heat event on November 18.(via @nvtnp_) https://t.co/hbAlRKP4A4 October 21, 2026
How much of an actual, full-on show Rockstar has constructed here, I cannot say. Remedy has done similar things with its games, but those are just brief snippets delivering a little bit of meta narrative ; Rockstar, by comparison, gave us multiple stand-up comedy shows in GTA 5 and black-and-white films in Red Dead Redemption 2… not to mention, fully animated horse testicles . In that light, is it hard to believe they may have created an entire animated series for GTA 6?
It might just be another blast from the GTA marketing machine—Rockstar is also literally renting the Miami Heat to promote its game, after all. At this point I don't think anything's off the table.
PlayStation and Xbox owners will find out in less than a week: Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19. A PC release date (or any kind of PC announcement at all) remains elusive.

title: Microsoft ‘deeply’ apologizes for global service outage, says no AI or hackers are to blame
author: Lincoln Carpenter
text:
Microsoft has issued an apology for the global services outage that began on November 12, which disrupted access to Microsoft 365 products for governments, hospitals, schools, and businesses around the world. The corporation says that neither AI nor malicious actors were at fault, but that the outage occurred as a result of an underlying infrastructural issue introduced during a network upgrade.
"We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously," Microsoft said. "We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services."
We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration.We will provide a full post-incident report once our review is complete. November 13, 2026
While popular speculation has been eager to attribute the outage to vibe-coding—and I can't blame anyone for speculating, considering Microsoft's push for company-wide AI adoption —the corporation says the outage was "a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents." It's unclear whether another word was meant to follow "cyber." I'm just telling you what the company wrote.
"The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change," Microsoft said, casually brutalizing the syntax of causality. "We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions."
Microsoft acknowledged that the restoration of service was slower than many might have hoped, but said that it brought services back online gradually to ensure stability.
Even if AI wasn't to blame for this week's outage, it's tempting to wonder whether any of the 10,000 employees Microsoft laid off in 2023 as part of its ongoing cost-cutting strategy might have known how to avoid the costly hiccup. Or any of the 6,000 employees it laid off in May 2025. Or the 9,000 it laid off that July. Or the 4,800 it laid off a year later, including 1,600 at Xbox with another 1,600 to follow. Or the 60,000 employees it extended voluntary buyout offers to last month.
Ah, well. No way to know. Microsoft said it will provide a more detailed incident report once its internal review of the outage is complete.

title: A survival game we once called 'Stalker and Tarkov's alien baby' is closing down less than a year after launch
author: Andy Chalk
text:
Pioner, a survival-shooter we said looked like " Stalker and Tarkov's alien baby " when we first laid eyes on it in 2021, is ending development and closing down. In an announcement posted today on Steam, developer GFAGames said further work on the game and continued operation of its servers requires more money, and it just doesn't have any.
"Over the past few months, we have been in talks with existing and potential partners about investment and new ways of working together that would allow us to preserve the project and the team," the studio wrote.
"We were unable to agree on the funding needed to continue the project. The studio no longer has sufficient funds of its own to continue development and keep the servers running."
Pioner looked promising when it turned up at the PC Gaming Show in 2021: A mash-up of Stalker, Metro, and Escape From Tarkov that featured both a singleplayer campaign and online co-op and PvP survival action, all of it built around late Soviet-era technology.
It launched into early access in December 2025 and worked its way to a peak concurrent player count of 1,686 on Steam a few months later—not huge, but far from catastrophic, and trending in the right direction.
Those numbers tailed off badly over the summer, though, as the dev team struggled with technical issues and updates came at a much slower pace than promised. August saw player counts collapse almost completely, and by mid-September only a couple dozen people were still playing.
Numerous replies to the shutdown announcement call for refunds to be issued, but GFAGames hasn't commented on those demands at this point. It also hasn't said when the game will actually be taken offline—I've reached out to ask and will update if I receive a reply.

title: Don't like AI in games? Crimson Desert studio Pearl Abyss ain't care: it's expanding AI use 'throughout our entire development pipeline'
author: Andy Chalk
text:
Earlier this year, Pearl Abyss apologized for the presence of AI-generated art in Crimson Desert—not because it had used generative AI, mind, but because players saw it. And it seems like the odds we might see more of it in the future are going up, as the studio said in its Q3 2026 earnings letter (via Eurogamer ) that it will be going even deeper on AI-powered development in the future.
The first reference to AI comes midway through the letter: "While we previously validated game systems only after implementing them manually, we now utilize AI to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," it states. "This enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed."
The studio immediately clarified, though, that AI "serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity," and that gameplay and content development "remain fully driven by our development team."
The future will see more of the same, with the same caveats. "We are integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality," Pearl Abyss writes. "AI is being utilized across various stages of development—including the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimization—and we are expanding its implementation throughout our entire development pipeline.
"We view AI not as a substitute for human developers, but as a tool to elevate development efficiency and quality. We will continue to expand our application of AI to deliver higher-fidelity games to the market more expeditiously."
That essentially repeats what Pearl Abyss said in February when players discovered the presence of generative AI art in Crimson Desert : It acknowledged that "some 2D visual props" had been created by AI during the early stages of development, but said they were supposed to be replaced "following final work and review by our art and development teams, with work that aligned with our quality standards and creative direction."
The studio also admitted that it had not "clearly disclosed our use of AI" in the development process, and promised to be more transparent about it in the future. This letter certainly could be seen as a step in that direction.
Pearl Abyss also said it aims to release DokeV, the " weird GTA: Babies game " revealed in 2021, sometime in the second half of 2028.

title: Yes, some brave games are still launching on Steam during GTA 6 week
author: Lincoln Carpenter
text:
Though it might seem hard to believe given its inescapability, not everyone is going to be playing GTA 6 next week. Some might be waiting for its eventual PC release (whenever that ends up being). Others might simply be unwilling to spend over a thousand dollars on a console just to enjoy the privilege.
Most publishers and developers releasing a videogame this season, however, have opted to vacate the GTA 6 blast radius—but not all of them. If you're looking for something new to play next week, you'll be pleased to know there are some brave games still launching on Steam. Here are some options to consider if you aren't dropping into Vice City:
Crusader Kings 3: Silk and Silver
(Image credit: Paradox) If you're a CK3 player—and you should be; it's number eight on our Top 100 list for a reason—then Paradox's next expansion should be on your radar. While everyone else is focused on Grand Theft Auto, you could be engaging in the grandest theft of all: Commerce.
Silk and Silver is all about mercantilism: Merchant families can jockey for trade route monopolies and use their wealth to lobby for influence, while new Republic governments offer patrician dynasties a venue to vie for dominance in the constitutional Assembly—potentially forming commercial or military pacts with other Republics. It's also got a lot of Italian content in it. Everyone loves Italian content.
Crusader Kings 3: Silk and Silver launches on November 17.
Spirit Crossing
(Image credit: Spry Fox) Among the cozier offerings arriving on Steam during GTA 6 week, Spirit Crossing is a building, crafting, and decorating MMO set in a world seemingly populated entirely by art students and befriendable spirits.
Borrowing a page from Sky: Children of the Light, it's only as much of an MMO as you want it to be: other players are only fully visible in your world if you mutually choose to engage with one another. Otherwise, you're free to roam its pastel soulscape and build out your own little corner of paradise solo for as long as you prefer.
Spirit Crossing launches on November 16.
Harma
(Image credit: Astrolabe Games) Listen. I know. It's 2026. I feel the same suspicions that you do when you see a game with full-on pixel illustrations like this on Steam nowadays. But the developers of Harma insist that it's "developed entirely by human creators and does not contain any contents or assets generated by AI tools." Which is good, because it looks neat, and I want to believe.
It's a roguelike deckbuilder that has both a story-driven campaign and a replayable "Dimensional Rift" mode, which should provide plenty of opportunity to continue admiring the work of its pixel artists. Assuming there were, in fact, pixel artists. They wouldn't lie to me, right? Please?
Harma launches in early access on November 16.
Melvor Idle 2
(Image credit: Jagex) Melvor Idle is for one of the most particular types of guys, and whether or not you're one of them should be clarified as soon as I say this sentence: Melvor Idle 2 is like Old School RuneScape with all the parts that aren't a skill grind stripped away. It's 100% gathering items so you can get better at gathering items so you can gather better items. It's pure, uncut clicking and waiting as numbers go up.
It's so thoroughly for RuneScape guys that, after the success of the first Melvor Idle, Jagex brought the operation under its publishing wing. If that's for you, I'm not judging. In many ways, you're living a more honest life than I am.
Melvor Idle 2 launches in early access on November 17.
Trafficity
(Image credit: Onramp Games) If you do not yet acknowledge the awesome power of the roundabout, it is time to learn. Trafficity is a game about traffic. There are cars, and they must go places. But only so many cars can go to one place at once.
This is the crux on which our world is both built and broken.
And now it is yours to solve—using a toolkit of gridless road design tools, fully-customizable traffic lights, and dynamic interchange simulation. Somewhere, in another game, your uncouth lessers are disrupting this great task with the stealing and crashing of your vehicular charges. But now, you answer to a higher calling. The traffic must flow.
Trafficity launches on November 16.
Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed
(Image credit: Devolver Digital) Publisher Devolver Digital is taking Grand Theft Auto 6 on directly with this fake remake (re-fake?) of an "unreleased" platformer starring its bizarre mascot, Volvy. Titled Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, the game challenges players to traverse four zany platforming worlds, using Volvy's grotesquely swollen hand to smash enemies, punch through blocks, and fist-i-copter across gaps.
While Volvy's Adventure boils down to a playable joke, it is a pretty stylish one. Developer doinksoft has clearly put a lot of care into the game's crisp retro pixel art, while the platforming seems to have a decent amount of physicality to it. The game will release on the same day as Grand Theft Auto six at a discounted price, so it'll be interesting to see whether it can cut through the noise of Vice City's hyper-real traffic.
Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed launches on November 19.

title: Indiana Jones and the Great Circle once had a Grand Theft Auto inspired wanted system, because MachineGames was 'afraid' players would kill all the Nazis 'with just guns'
author: Rick Lane
text:
Indiana Jones and The Great Circle offered such a great depiction of everyone's favourite Nazi thumping archaeologist that it's hard to imagine developer MachineGames building that game any differently. Yet according to design director Jens Andersson, getting the Indy feel of The Great Circle right represented a significant challenge for the Swedish studio.
One of the hardest problems MachineGames struggled with was the presence of guns in the game, specifically how to stop players from just blasting through armies of Nazis without making guns less fun to use. Speaking to FRVR , Andersson explained that having satisfying firearms in The Great Circle was "non-negotiable" as "we have a lot of people at Machine[Games] that love guns".
Since MachineGames wanted The Great Circle to be true to Spielberg's films, they needed guns to be a part of Indy's toolset and not the default response to every problem. One partial solution was to make reloading slow, encouraging players to use other tools like Indy's whip or his fists, but this alone wasn't enough.
"We had so many designs to try and get around that," Andersson continued. "For example, a GTA star level system when you shoot someone and reinforcements [start] coming in." The thinking here seems to have been to discourage players from going overboard with using loud weapons. "Because we were so afraid that this would be the default thing that the player would do. They take down a guy, they see a gun on the floor, and they clear the whole area with just guns."
In the end, the solution MachineGames stumbled upon was to provide alternative, breakable melee weapons ranging from frying pans to violins. These abundant, lightly comedic tools encouraged players to embrace the improvisational nature of how Indy fights, offering a quick knockout both in stealth and when the player's ammunition ran dry.
Remarkably, Andersson says that breakable weapons "got in very late" during development. But when the studio "saw how effective it was, that's when we started putting all this weird stuff in. The violin, all of this weird stuff that makes it a little slapstick-y, but not slapstick."
This system proved instrumental in getting the final balance of Indy's combat right, where stealth and fisticuffs are the primary approach, while guns tend to be a last resort. "We penalised shooting so much in that game. I know a lot of people are frustrated about that, but many more people love it," Andersson says. "The thing that really fixed it was that we made melee combat so interesting, fun, and easy. Not easy challenge-wise, but just it's easy to get into. You stealth up, you hit someone from behind, the breakable weapon system was super important to do that. 'Oh, there's a new weapon, it's a fly swatter, I want to try this.'"
Ultimately, Indy's dynamic combat was a bit part of what made it Machine Games' best game to date, earning it a score of 86 in PC Gamer's Indiana Jones and the Great Circle Review . Whether we'll see another Indy game from Machine Games is still up in the air. But if it does happen, it probably won't be soon, as the studio has just confirmed that's it's working on Wolfenstein 3 .

title: 40% of game developers use generative AI according to a new report, but more than half reckon the technology has a negative impact on the games industry
author: Rick Lane
text:
Use of generative AI remains one of the most contentious topics in the games industry. Developers who see a bright new future in the tech have increasingly clashed with those concerned by the ethical , artistic and labour implications tools like ChatGPT and Claude Opus bring to the medium. The divisive nature of the subject was starkly revealed in a new report, which calculated that 40% of game developers are actively using generative AI, while more than half of developers believe LLMs and agentic coding tools have a negative impact on the industry.
These were the conclusions of the latest State of the Game Industry report from the Game Developer's Conference (via Eurogamer ). The report surveyed over 2,600 respondents from all corners of the industry. Of those surveyed, 40% of respondents said they used generative AI as part of their job, a slight increase from 36% from last year .
Of those surveyed, the report found that older professionals were more likely to use generative AI, with 54% of workers over 45 stating they use the tech. The report also states that men were more likely to use AI tools than women, and that indie developers were less likely to use it than studios working on premium, free-to-play, and mobile-exclusive games.
Among those who have embraced generative AI, the most common use of it was for research and brainstorming. Nearly three-quarters of AI advocates said they use it for this function, while over half (56%) said they use it for code generation and debugging. Use of generative AI seems to drop sharply for tasks viewed as being more creative, however, with 22% saying they use it for concept art and visual ideation, and only 7% using it for player-facing features.
(Image credit: Panic) Although use of generative AI has increased, the perception of the technology's impact on the industry remains predominately negative. 55% of those surveyed said that generative AI is having a negative effect on the games industry, an increase of 1% from the start of 2026, and up 25% from 2025. Meanwhile, 35% said the impact was mixed, with only 8% believing that generative AI is having a positive effect.
The report concludes (with the help of AI 'sentiment analysis' tools, it should be noted) that games industry professionals are "forming more nuanced view on generative AI, rather than taking an all-or-nothing stance". At the same time, the report highlighted new concerns that AI use leads to "skill atrophy and loss in professional and personal development" while developers are taking a dimmer view of "using generative AI for player-facing features."
There are other factors that explain the increase in AI usage alongside a growing negative sentiment. Whether you are pro or anti AI, the tech is becoming harder to avoid. A casual Google search in 2026 technically counts as using AI, regardless of how you feel about the presence or quality of the resulting AI summary. At the same time, the effects of AI on the games industry—particularly agentic coding tools—have become more pronounced in 2026. Platforms like Steam and itch are wrestling to deal with a dramatic increase in AI slop games, while use of the tech among developers has triggered heated debates in spaces like the IGF awards.
It will be interesting to see how these opinions shift in the next twelve months, given the current situation within the broader AI industry. After years of unprecedented growth, big tech has been rocked by a series of scandals and growing doubt among investors about the long-term profitability of generative tools. Will 2027 be the year that the so-called 'AI bubble' finally bursts? And if it does, how will that impact the proliferation of generative AI among the games industry and tech more broadly?

title: Formula 1 just found a bizarre financial supporter in horse girl gacha Umamusume: Pretty Derby
author: Mollie Taylor
text:
What is Formula 1 if not just very fast, mechanical horse racing? Surely I'm not the only one who has asked that question, especially considering the Japanese Grand Prix leg of the 2027 F1 World Championship has just revealed that Cygame's horse girl gacha Umamusume: Pretty Derby has become a founding partner.
What does that mean in practice? Well, according to a press release, founding partners are "the highest tier supporters of the F1 Japanese Grand Prix," where they "bring additional value to the event while helping to shape the direction of its growth. Through marketing, promotional activities, and creating new experiences for fans, Umamusume will continue contributing to the long term growth of the Japanese Grand Prix."
(Image credit: Cygames, Inc.) In layman's terms, that'll be a tidy sum of money invested into the Japanese Grand Prix, and in Umamusume's case it also means slapping its name on one of Suzuka Circuit's iconic corners—changing the name from the 130R corner to Umamusume 130R for around a year. Unsurprisingly, there'll also be a bit of Umamusume marketing and branding splashed across a banner or two, though Cygames says that none of it will be on display during the actual Japanese Grand Prix itself.
(I'm also learning today that F1 circuit corners have names. Neat.)
In case you're not familiar with Umamusume's whole schtick, it's an anime-slash-gacha-game all about anthropomorphised horse girls. Ones who are also based on real-life race horses, by the by. The gacha's global release brought tons of eyes onto the franchise last year, and its fans have done an awful lot of good—stuff like donating so much grass to the horse girl's real-life counterparts that it broke the donation website , or raising hundreds of thousands of dollars towards renovating stables.
It's a fun little collaboration between two vastly different sports, and I imagine there's definitely a good chunk of folks who sit in the Venn diagram of "F1 fan" and "horse girl fan". For those who do lie firmly in between those two fandoms, Cygames is also opening a special booth at Suzuka Circuit, as well as a mysterious "special live music performance" taking place on April 10. Considering Umamusume has plenty of original music (since it's also kind of an idol game… it's hard to explain, okay?) I wouldn't be surprised if we'll be hearing a ditty or two from the likes of Silence Suzuka and Special Week.

title: Halo: Campaign Evolved is getting Firefight as a free update, though I'm not sure it'll do much to change the remake's fortunes
author: Rick Lane
text:
Xbox has announced the first update for Halo: Campaign Evolved since August, one which will add Firefight to the remake's overhaul of the original game's story.
Firefight is Halo's cooperative PvE mode which debuted in Halo 3: ODST . It's a round-based defence affair where players must survive as long as possible against increasingly dangerous waves of enemies. Following ODST, the mode appeared in every subsequent Halo game with the exception of Halo 4, which featured a mode called Spartan Ops instead.
In its announcement , Xbox was extremely light on details regarding the addition of Firefight. But the company said it'll share "additional details" about the Firefight update during Halo Fest, which takes place over the weekend commencing December 12.
I'm pleased to see Campaign Evolved getting some more features, but the announcement also increases my sense that Xbox really doesn't know what to do with Halo at present. Campaign Evolved itself felt like a collective shrug from Halo Studios, a glossy but unambitious overhaul of the original game, with three new levels that nobody liked and shorn of the multiplayer that the PC version so enjoyable in the early 2000s.
Morgan Park felt similarly in his Halo: Campaign Evolved Review . "It was cool to see another interpretation of a game special to me, but the glitzy coat of paint primarily highlights how right Bungie got it in 2001, and how its modern stewards are nudging Halo in an unremarkable direction," he wrote back in July.
A Firefight mode, coming nearly six months after launch with almost complete radio silence since August, smacks more of "We need something for Halo Fest" than the start of a bright new future for the remake. Not that I expected it to magically rejuvenate Halo. But that lack of expectation, of anticipation, is in itself part of the problem.
I could be wrong, of course. As part of Xbox's "reset"—which has included laying off thousands of staff and saying sayonara to several studios—Xbox also handed control of Halo over to Activision . So perhaps bringing back Firefight is the first step in Activision's plan—whatever that is. Some have suggested that Xbox wants Halo to be a more Call of Duty -like experience, which would certainly make sense from Xbox's perspective. Whether Halo can actually be that is, of course, another matter entirely.
